jobs.title: Project Manager (PMP Certified) Exp-5+ Years
jobs.description:
Company Description
techvantage.ai helps organizations solve complex business problems and accelerate innovation by leveraging the full spectrum of AI, from advanced analytics and machine learning to enterprise-scale automation. The company focuses on embedding intelligence into core business operations to unlock new efficiencies and capabilities. As pioneers in Agentic AI, techvantage.ai builds autonomous systems that sense, decide, and act, enabling enterprises to respond dynamically to changing demands. The organization partners with leading companies in Banking, Financial Services, Insurance, Telecom, Media, Retail, and Automotive to deliver solutions that drive agility and breakthrough results. Team members join a forward-looking environment that shapes the next generation of intelligent enterprise automation.
Role Description
This is a full-time remote role for a Project Manager (PMP Certified) with 5+ years of experience. The Project Manager will lead end-to-end delivery of AI and automation projects, including planning, scoping, resource allocation, risk management, and stakeholder communication. Daily responsibilities include coordinating cross-functional teams, managing project timelines and budgets, tracking milestones, and ensuring adherence to quality standards and compliance requirements. The role involves facilitating meetings, preparing project documentation and status reports, resolving issues and dependencies, and aligning project outcomes with business objectives. The Project Manager will work closely with technical and business stakeholders to prioritize initiatives, manage change requests, and support continuous improvement of project management practices.
Qualifications

Strong Project Management skills, including planning, execution, risk management, and stakeholder communication.
Experience with Expeditor and Expediting responsibilities to ensure timely delivery of tasks, materials, and project outputs.
Knowledge of Inspection processes to validate deliverables, quality standards, and compliance with project requirements.
Ability to handle Logistics Management for project resources, coordination across teams, and alignment of schedules.
Active PMP certification and 5+ years of experience managing technology or AI-related projects.
Proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Jira, Asana, MS Project) and standard frameworks (e.g., PMBOK, Agile).
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience collaborating in distributed and remote teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related field; experience in AI, data, or automation domains is an advantage.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Southwest
jobs.description:
Your Job

DEPCOM Power, a leading renewable energy EPC firm, is seeking a Project Manager for the Southwest portfolio to lead the execution of utility-scale Solar PV, Battery Energy Storage, and Repowering projects from pre-construction through commissioning and closeout.

As a Project Manager, you will create long-term value by leading project teams that deliver safe, reliable, and profitable results. You will apply Principle Based Management to strengthen ownership, improve execution discipline, make sound economic decisions, and build trusted customer and stakeholder relationships from pre-construction through closeout.

This is a remote role that requires travel to field construction project sites at a frequency between 25% - 50% dependent on project need.

Our Team

DEPCOM's Project Delivery Organization executes turnkey PV, Battery Energy Storage, and Repower projects, including collection substations and generation transmission lines. The team partners with vendors, subcontractors, utilities, and internal capabilities to deliver disciplined project execution and strong customer outcomes nationwide.

What You Will Do

Lead project teams to deliver safe, reliable, and profitable outcomes across scope, schedule, cost, quality, compliance, and customer expectations.
Develop and execute project plans, forecasts, risk mitigation strategies, and phase-gate deliverables from pre-construction through commissioning and closeout.
Apply economic thinking to evaluate cost, risk, schedule, and value tradeoffs while making timely decisions that improve project outcomes.
Build and develop high-performing teams by setting clear expectations, coaching for contribution, and aligning strengths to project and business needs.
Coordinate customers, subcontractors, vendors, utilities, consultants, and internal partners to support transparent communication and disciplined execution.
Strengthen customer and stakeholder relationships by resolving challenges, honoring commitments, and creating mutual long-term value.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

Experience managing EPC, industrial, infrastructure, utility scale renewable energy, or large capital projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars
Experience managing project scope, schedule, cost, forecasting, risk mitigation, contracts, or customer commitments.
Experience leading project teams, subcontractors, vendors, or cross-functional stakeholders.
Valid US driver's license.
Legal authorization to work permanently in the United States for any employer without requiring a visa transfer or visa sponsorship now or in the future.

What Will Put You Ahead

EPC experience in Utility Solar, Wind, BESS, conventional power or industrial projects.
Experience leading self-perform construction execution on large or complex projects.
Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
PMP, CCM, PE, or other relevant project management or construction industry certifications.
Experience partnering with Business Development, Estimating, Operations, or customers to support project pursuits, repeat business, and executable project solutions.

For this role, we anticipate paying $150K - $200K per year. This role is eligible for variable pay, issued as a monetary bonus or in another form.

At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.

Hiring Philosophy

All Koch companies value diversity of thought, perspectives, aptitudes, experiences, and backgrounds. We are Military Ready and Second Chance employers. Learn more about our hiring philosophy here .

Who We Are

As a Koch Engineered Solutions company, DEPCOM Power is a leading energy solutions partner for the utility solar and broader energy industries, providing project development support, engineering, procurement and construction, energy storage, repowering and operations and maintenance services. Our highly skilled team of conventional and renewable power industry experts work to deliver the lowest cost of energy and the highest rate of return.

At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company.

Our Benefits

Our goal is for each employee, and their families, to live fulfilling and healthy lives. We provide essential resources and support to build and maintain physical, financial, and emotional strength - focusing on overall wellbeing so you can focus on what matters most. Our benefits plan includes - medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, ADD, disability, retirement, paid vacation/time off, educational assistance, and may also include infertility assistance, paid parental leave and adoption assistance. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. If you have questions on what benefits apply to you, please speak to your recruiter.

Additionally, everyone has individual work and personal needs. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results.

Equal Opportunities

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status. Except where prohibited by state law, some offers of employment are conditioned upon successfully passing a drug test. jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
At Tucuvi, we help healthcare organizations ensure every patient receives timely high-quality care by augmenting clinical teams with AI.

Our clinical-grade AI Care Management platform automates and orchestrates high-volume workflows end to end, combining autonomous AI agents including LOLA, our Voice Clinical Agent with workflow logic, escalation, documentation, and seamless integration into existing health system infrastructure. Built for trust and clinical reality, Tucuvi is the first Class IIb Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) for Voice AI driven patient management.

Today, we support 50+ care pathways across 80+ healthcare organizations, delivering up to 80% automation of nursing workflows, >90% patient engagement, and improved clinical outcomes. We recently raised $20M in Series A funding to scale across Europe and the US.

CONTEXT

We expand care team capacity by executing agentic voice workflows for pharmacy refill outreach, post-discharge follow-up, care-gap closure, chronic care check-ins, and scheduling, among others. The common thread is high-volume workflows where clinical teams can't keep up with the outreach patients need.

You don't need deep clinical expertise in every pathway. You will be supported by clinical subject-matter experts, Solutions Engineers, and a Product team in Madrid who own protocol design, conversation flows, and escalation logic. What you need is the operating discipline to take what they build, deploy it inside a real health system, prove with data that it's working, and build the case for what comes next.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Your mission is to turn our US health system partnerships into programs that deliver measurable outcomes, expand into new use cases, and become the reference accounts that open the next ten doors. This role requires up to 25–30% travel for go-lives, strategic reviews, and onsite work with customer teams.

You'll own the full lifecycle of a health system relationship from the first site implementation through multi-site expansion and new use case discovery. You'll work directly with care managers, nurses, call center staff, and pharmacy techs as well as decision-makers from directors to VP-level champions. You're the person the customer calls first, and the person who shapes what they ask for next.

Internally, you'll translate what you learn on the ground into product priorities, expansion strategies, and the evidence that makes our next sale easier. You are the operator who makes the program work and the strategist who makes it grow.

You bring the structure, the rigor, the commercial instinct, and the accountability our customers need to maintain a thriving program.

We're growing rapidly in the US, so you will have room for career progression and development.

WHAT TO EXPECT FURING YOUR FIRST MONTHS WITH US

During the first 3 months:
Onboarding and training to get you up to speed on our platform, our workflows, and the accounts you'll own. You'll be running site implementations independently well by month three: kick-off meetings, workflow mapping sessions with clinical staff, platform configuration alongside our clinical and product team, go-live, and first-line support. You'll also be building relationships with the director-level champions who will determine whether these accounts expand.

From month 3 to 6:
You will run multiple concurrent deployments and own the KPI reporting cadence for your accounts. You should be able tell the difference between a metric that's noisy and a metric that's telling you something. You're actively identifying where the next use case or site expansion sits and starting to build the case for it using the customer's data.

By month 12:
You've driven at least one account expansion beyond the initial scope. You've turned what you learned into a repeatable rollout and growth model. You're the person the customer's VP level leadership trusts to tell them what's working, what isn't, and what to do next and the person our Sales team brings into new opportunities because your accounts are the proof.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Drive account growth, not just delivery.
You own activation end to end but the job doesn't end at go-live. You identify expansion opportunities (new sites, new use cases, new pathways), build the business case with the customer's outcomes data, and partner with Sales to close. Delivery is how we earn the right to grow.

Frame the case for leadership.
When a health system's VP asks "is this working and should we expand," you don't hand them a dashboard, you build the narrative: what the data says, what it means, what you'd recommend, and what it would take. This is the skill that turns a single-site pilot into a system-wide program.

Own the workflow translation between the customer and our product team.
You observe how clinical teams actually work from call flow, cadence, handoff logic, edge cases, and bring that back with enough specificity that our Clinical and Product teams can build the right thing. You make sure the people who do have what they need from the field, and you own whether the result holds up once it's live.

Define and measure the KPIs that matter.
Own the metrics for your accounts reach rate, engagement, confirmation rate, escalation volume, staff time freed, clinical outcomes and know what "good" looks like for each. Spot the trends before anyone asks, and translate usage data into a value story the health system's leadership will use to justify the next investment.

Build and maintain VP-level champion relationships.
The directors and VPs who sponsor your programs are the people who decide whether this account doubles or plateaus. You cultivate those relationships deliberately not just with delivery results, but with strategic insight about what their organization should do next.

Build trust with clinical staff.
LOLA only works if the people using it believe in it. You're the person in the room earning the respect of clinicians by listening well, responding fast, and proving it with outcomes.

Own the feedback loop to Product and Engineering.
Distinguish a bug from a real feature gap from scope creep, and bring it back to the team with enough clarity that they can act on it. Your field perspective directly shapes what gets built next.

Scale with efficiency.
Manage concurrent workstreams without compromising quality, and turn what you learn into processes and playbooks other people can run.

REQUIREMENTS

8–12 years of relevant experience, with a track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder programs end to end including at least one where you drove expansion or growth beyond the original scope, not just delivered it.

Previous experience in one or more of the following (helpful):

Strategic account management or client partnership at a healthcare technology or services company

Health system program management implementation, expansion planning, change management, or process design

Clinical workflow redesign, care transformation, or process improvement inside a hospital or health system

Growth instinct, not just delivery discipline.
You've spotted the adjacent opportunity, built the case, and acted not waited for someone to ask. In interviews, we'll ask you to walk us through a specific example.

Strong, demonstrable project management skills.
You build the plan, you run the plan, you know where every dependency sits. Multiple parallel workstreams without losing control.

You lead with scoping, not assumptions.
Your first move in a new account is to map the process, identify the gaps between what was sold and what's real, and adjust the plan before problems find you.

Comfort building a financial narrative.
You can translate operational metrics into a business case a VP will act on. If you've built an ROI model or an expansion proposal for a client, that's a strong signal.

A self-service-first approach to problem solving.
You try it before you ask about it.

US-based, with up to 25–30% travel for go-lives, strategic reviews, and onsite work. You'll also work in close partnership with our Spain-based team, bringing a US perspective to Tucuvi as we continue building it into a truly global healthtech company.

WHAT WE’LL ASK YOU TO SHOW US

A program or customer you grew beyond its original scope what you identified, how you built the case, and what happened

A project plan you built and ran not one you inherited

A problem you caught before it escalated, and the signal that tipped you off

THIS IS NOT THE ROLE FOR YOU IF

You think the job ends at go-live

You deliver scope but don't look for what comes next

You aren't interested in helping design a better repeatable playbook for others

You measure success in tickets closed, not outcomes achieved

You'd rather escalate the hard conversation with clinical staff than have it

You need to be the domain expert rather than the person who makes domain experts effective

WHAT WE OFFER

$140K–$160K base + variable + equity (based on experience)

Remote work (Boston, NYC, West Coast preferred)

Flexible working hours

Team buildings (at least tw...

jobs.title: Project Manager - Stormwater
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we challenge- what’s accepted, so we can shape innovative and lasting solutions for tomorrow. If you’re interested in a long and rewarding career working with one of the highest ranked design firms in ENR’s list of Top 500 Design Firms, and with the industry’s best and most innovative engineers, then Jacobs is where you belong. We are looking for an enthusiastic and highly-motivated team member to work on a variety of stormwater collection and conveyance, wastewater collection and conveyance, and site civil design projects as a Project Manager in our water market. Are you ready to take your career to the next level? By joining our team you’ll have the opportunity to lead the planning and design of wastewater and stormwater collection and conveyance systems and assist more senior engineers on larger, more complex projects. This position will support both local and national wastewater and stormwater projects. As part of our growing team, you’ll be responsible for performing all aspects of engineering. We are looking for a passionate team member who has a good understanding of engineering principles, theories, and concepts and has a desire to work on the planning, design and construction of wastewater conveyance, stormwater conveyance, green stormwater infrastructure, and site civil projects. We’re seeking self-motivated professionals with a desire to grow personally as well as professionally with each project in our diverse and fast-paced office. If you’re up for the challenge, we’ve been looking for someone just like you. Join us and we will support you in continuing the development of your skills and exploring all that you can do across our global company, with opportunities to share your knowledge along the way.

Here's What You’ll Be Doing

Collaborate and work with a multi-disciplinary team in the delivery of wastewater, water resources, and site civil design projects.
Conduct preliminary engineering by analyzing data, performing calculations, and evaluating options to develop the best solution and make recommendation.
Autonomously evaluate and improve the selection and/or modification of standard techniques, procedures, criteria, and systems to efficiently meet project goals.
Technical writing, reviewing, and providing clear, concise input to investigations, memorandums, or solutions reports.
Prepare drawings and specifications as well as changes to drawings based on engineering staff and supervisor markups, edits, QA/QC comments and/or suggestions.
Communicate and coordinate information with other engineering disciplines and company offices.
Review work performed by others for adequacy on completion.
Attend project meetings, coordinate work with project team members, supervisor/client.
Interface directly with our clients.
Mentor and support junior staff in the local and regional water group.
Participate in professional organizations for marketing, industry recognition, networking, and building the Jacobs brand.
Position may include supervision of one or more project engineers as a task manager on a large project, or as a project manager of small projects.

At Jacobs, we’re partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other. Jacobs’ health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Typical benefits offered include flexible work schedules and opportunities to work remotely, educational reimbursement, retirement benefits, employee stock purchase plan, health benefits, disability benefits, life and accident insurance, voluntary benefits, paid time off and paid holidays, and parental leave.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelors Degree in Civil, Water Resources, or Environmental Engineering
Virginia PE license or have the ability to obtain within six months of hire
Ability to efficiently utilize time in executing assigned tasks accurately and within schedule
Proficient knowledge of MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint)
Ability and desire to use production tools, such as ESRI ArcGIS, AutoCAD, computer graphic and design programs, and hydraulic modeling software
Applied knowledge of basic engineering principles and prescribed methods
Analytical and technical problem-solving skills
Self-motivation, team-oriented work practices, top-notch organizational skills, and the ability to effectively multi-task in a fast-paced environment
Working knowledge and understanding of local and state design codes and standards
At least 5 years of professional experience in water resources engineering and related experience
This position is based in Richmond, VA. To be eligible, candidates must be able to regularly attend meetings and perform field activities in the greater Richmond metro region.

Ideally, Here’s What You’ll Also Have

Master’s degree in Civil, Water Resources, or Environmental Engineering
Project or task management experience
Academic or professional background in water resources, hydraulics/fluid mechanics/hydrology, as well as wastewater processes preferred
Experience in serving various clients involving a wide variety of fields including wastewater, stormwater, and site civil

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has a U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $125,000.00 to $170,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on March 19, 2025. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.title: Sr Project Manager - AI Data Centers
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

This job opportunity is available at ANY location in the United States. Ideally, selected candidates will be near a JACOBS U.S. based office, but we intend to hire the "best" candidates.

Your impact

Jacobs is the #1-ranked design firm on ENR’s Top 500 Design Firms list — for the seventh consecutive year — and the #1 Program Management firm globally (ENR, 2025). We are not riding the data center wave; we are engineering it. Jacobs’ Data Center Digital Twin solution, built on NVIDIA’s Omniverse DSX Blueprint, was highlighted in Jensen Huang’s GTC keynote in March 2026, placing Jacobs at the technical frontier of gigawatt-scale AI factory design.

This is your opportunity to elevate your career to the next level — leading complex, multi-discipline programs as a Senior Project Manager (CA) Lead, across OE, EPCM, and Design-Build delivery, working alongside the most recognized hyperscale owners, colocation operators, and advanced manufacturing clients in the industry. At Jacobs, you will do what you are most passionate about, at a scale and with a client roster that defines the future of AI infrastructure. You will manage engineering-side project execution from basis of design through IFC, construction administration, commissioning, and turnover. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, manage scope, schedule, budget, fee, risk, quality, client commitments, and field coordination—while serving as the connection between design intent and site execution.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Controls

Own the project management plan scope, schedule, budget, fee forecasting, staffing, contract administration, risk register, and change controls across the delivery lifecycle.
Develop and maintain project execution plans, deliverable lists, staffing plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and client reporting; monitor progress and implement recovery actions when needed.
Manage Jacobs engineering fee budgets, subcontract scopes, cost-at-completion, variances, change orders, and commercial impacts with appropriate project-controls support.
Lead schedule development in P6, MS Project, or comparable tools; coordinate critical-path milestones across BOD, 30%/60%/IFC design, permits, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
Delivery, Construction Administration & Technical Coordination
Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams from concept through construction administration across Civil, Structural, MEP, process, controls, fire protection, and telecommunications/ICT systems, as assigned.
Serve as the primary coordination point among the client, Project Engineer, discipline design teams, construction management, commissioning teams, vendors, and subcontractors.
As Owner’s Engineer or CA lead, represent the client’s interests through design review, RFI response, submittal processing, construction observation, field issue resolution, document issuance, and schedule adherence.
Perform and coordinate field walks, engineering inspections, field checks, equipment and system verification, and line walkdowns; document observations with photos, sketches, markups, and action items.
Verify that installed conditions, equipment identification, tags, room names, system references, and drawing information are accurate, current, and traceable.
Manage RFIs, submittals, design changes, technical queries, nonconforming work, field change documentation, and potential change-order impacts through documented resolution.

Quality, Safety, Commissioning & Turnover

Enforce the Jacobs quality management plan; facilitate design QA/QC, constructability reviews, interdisciplinary coordination, and key issuance reviews at 30%/60%/IFP/IFC milestones.
Champion Jacobs BeyondZero® safety culture; review contractor safety plans and conduct site safety observations during construction-administration activities.
Support construction readiness, third-party testing, commissioning, integrated systems testing, punch-list development, system turnover, and operational handover.
Maintain complete, accurate, and auditable project records, including reports, inspection and test documentation, walkdown packages, redlines, RFIs, NCRs, meeting minutes, change logs, and closeout information.
Client Relationships & Growth
Serve as a primary client point of contact for assigned work; manage coordination meetings, dashboards, issue escalation, action closure, and executive-level communication as appropriate.
Support project staffing, onboarding, mentoring, lessons learned, continuous improvement, proposals, estimates, basis-of-estimate development, and client presentations.
Promote Jacobs’ culture of safety, quality, integrity, collaboration, and inclusion in all interactions with project teams, contractors, clients, and partners.

Here's what you'll need

Successful candidates
will possess substantial project management experience leading large-scale data center, mission-critical facility, industrial, construction, engineering, or similar physical infrastructure projects. This role is not focused on software development, enterprise IT programs, application implementation, network operations, cloud transformation, or technology product delivery. Applicants with predominantly IT Program Manager, Technical Program Manager, Software Project Manager, or SDLC-based experience should carefully review the infrastructure and construction requirements before applying.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or related discipline (or equivalent experience)
10 years or more of progressive project management, construction administration, engineering coordination, field engineering, or technical project-delivery experience on complex facilities
Demonstrated project-management or CA experience supporting Data Center, Advanced Technology, Semiconductor, mission-critical, industrial, or similarly complex facility projects; direct hyperscale experience is preferred
Fluency across at least one Jacobs delivery mode OE, EPCM, or Design-Build; ability to coordinate design, construction, commissioning, and client teams knowledge of project controls, including scheduling, cost tracking, fee forecasting, change management, risk, action tracking, and project reporting; proficiency with P6 or MS Project preferred

Preferred Qualifications

PMP (Project Management Professional) PMI certification preferred or in progress
Professional Engineer — Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, or Structural; multi-state reciprocity valued
Master’s degree in engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management

jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Technical Program Management Teams

The Technical Program Management team sits within Engineering Operations & Technical Program Management. Our TPMs are force multipliers, helping teams move faster, more effectively and with purpose. In Japan, you’ll be the only TPM on the ground, bridging Wayve’s global R&D with local delivery.

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Technical Program Manager for Robotaxi, you’ll own the programs that bring our robotaxi service to life, from vehicle and fleet readiness to on-the-ground launch and scaling in market. Based in Yokohama, you’ll work across autonomy, vehicle software, hardware, operations, safety and local partners to turn Wayve’s AI Driver into a safe, reliable robotaxi service, keeping complex, multi-team, cross-geography delivery predictable in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment. As the only TPM in Japan, you’ll also help support local vehicle hardware and software programs as needed.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Owning the lifecycle of robotaxi programs, from vehicle and fleet readiness to launch and in-market scaling, improving delivery through structured execution and coordination.
Tracking and managing dependencies, risks and trade-offs across autonomy, vehicle, operations and safety, and escalating early with clear options.
Keeping engineering, fleet operations, safety and local partner teams aligned, bridging Wayve’s global R&D with local delivery in Japan.
Providing hands-on program support for robotaxi launch and in-market operations, on the ground in Yokohama.
Supporting local vehicle hardware and software programs as needed, as the only TPM in Japan.
Running planning, stand-ups, reviews and retros that keep multi-team delivery predictable and reliable.
Communicating progress and risk to engineers, partners and senior leaders, tailoring updates to each audience.
Improving tooling, processes and ways of working, and sharing patterns across the TPM org.

Essential

🙌 You should apply if:

Bias for action: 5+ years leading complex, multi-team programs (or a strong record at this level). You lead high-complexity work across teams and get things done.
Technically strong across software and hardware: Credible with engineers across autonomy, vehicle software, and vehicle hardware; you reason about how the AI Driver runs as a robotaxi service on real vehicles - and can support vehicle hardware / software programs too - even though you won't write production code.
Stays neutral and adapts under pressure: Effective in ambiguous, safety-critical environments; you flex your style and bring structure without slowing delivery.
Strong project management: Skilled at planning, prioritising, and managing risk and dependencies across teams.
Exceptional communicator & collaborator: Operating from a remote office, you keep distributed teams aligned across time zones - communicating with clarity, proactively and in writing - and influence without authority across all stakeholders.
Cross-cultural & on the ground: Comfortable working across geographies and cultures, and hands-on with vehicles and operations in Japan; Japanese language skills a plus.
Generalist range: As the only TPM in-country, comfortable flexing beyond robotaxi to support vehicle hardware and software programs; happy wearing multiple hats.
Data-driven: Comfortable defining and using metrics to steer delivery and decisions.
Growth mindset: Open to feedback and always looking to improve.
Systems thinking: You reason about how the parts of a complex system fit together, and how a change in one area ripples into others.
Product-minded: You focus on outcomes and the people your programs serve - prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like, not just tracking activity.

Desirable

Robotaxi / AV operations, fleet, mobility, ride-hailing, or automotive experience; experience launching or scaling a service in market.
Exposure to ML, autonomy, or other compute-heavy / safety-critical domains; experience working across global and local teams. Japanese language skills and/or based in (or willing to relocate to) Yokohama / Tokyo.
An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency Interviews (TPM screen and technical & partnership interviews; 1 hour 45 mins total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (program design; 1 hour)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (30 mins).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

Wayve is committed to providing a fair and respectful recruitment process for all candidates, free from harassment and discrimination.

The Company has zero tolerance for sexual harassment against job applicants or similar individuals.

All communications relating to recruitment activities are conducted through the Company's recruitment system or using an email address with the Company's domain. Employees do not use their personal email addresses or social media accounts for recruitment-related communications.
Employees do not engage in private communications unrelated to recruitment activities, invite applicants to private meals, request or seek a personal or romantic relationship, or otherwise initiate private contact with applicants.
Sexual remarks or conduct, physical contact, questions concerning sexual matters, and any other conduct constituting harassment are prohibited.

If you have any concerns, you can contact our consultation desk at peoplepartners@wayve.ai. All consultations are treated with strict confidentiality, your privacy will be protected, and no one will be subject to any disadvantageous treatment for raising a concern or cooperating with an inquiry.

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

Senior Program Manager - Fixed term 12 month contract

Lead transformational programs that shape the future of Australia Post

At Australia Post, we're delivering change at scale. As a Senior Program Manager, you'll play a pivotal role in leading some of our largest and most strategically important business and technology programs, bringing together people, technology and operations to deliver meaningful outcomes for our customers, communities and workforce.
This is an opportunity for an experienced delivery leader who thrives on complexity, influence and impact. You'll lead end-to-end program delivery, guide multidisciplinary teams and partners, and work closely with senior leaders to bring Australia Post's strategic priorities to life.
What you'll be doing

As a Senior Program Manager, you'll be responsible for the successful delivery of large-scale transformation and technology programs from planning through to implementation and operational transition.
You'll:
Lead complex, enterprise-wide programs delivering strategic business outcomes
Develop and manage integrated program roadmaps, plans, budgets and delivery schedules
Drive governance, risk management, assurance and benefits realisation activities
Coordinate multiple projects, workstreams, business units, technology teams and delivery partners
Manage program financials, forecasts, vendors and commercial obligations
Resolve delivery challenges and navigate competing priorities across stakeholders
Provide executive-ready reporting, insights and recommendations
Ensure operational readiness and successful transition of program outcomes into business-as-usual operations
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, safety and continuous improvement

About You

You're a highly capable program leader who knows how to turn strategy into delivery outcomes.
You bring:
Extensive experience leading large, complex transformation and technology programs
Strong expertise across program planning, governance, budgeting, dependency management, delivery execution and benefits realisation
Experience managing significant budgets, vendors, contracts and delivery partners
A proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams across business, technology and operational environments
Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence and build trusted relationships at senior leadership levels
Experience recovering challenged programs and establishing clear delivery controls and recovery plans
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complexity into clear, actionable recommendations

Why join us?

At Australia Post, we're transforming how we connect Australians every day. You'll have the opportunity to work on programs that matter, collaborating with talented people across the enterprise while helping shape our future direction.
You'll be part of a culture that values:
Trust, inclusion, empowerment and safety
Customer-focused decision making
Continuous learning and growth
Collaborative leadership and One Team behaviours
Digital and data-informed thinking

What we're looking for

While not essential, relevant qualifications in Information Technology, Business, Management or a related discipline, along with recognised Program or Project Management certifications, will be highly regarded.
An understanding of Australia Post's strategy, systems, products and operations will also be advantageous.
Ready to lead change at enterprise scale? If you're passionate about delivering complex programs, building high-performing teams and creating lasting business impact, we'd love to hear from you.
Join us and help shape what's next for Australia Post.
🚚📦📨

What else is in it for you? 

Bring your whole self to work every day and be met by a welcoming bunch of people who respect and support you 
Flexible and hybrid working arrangements, like the opportunity to work from home two days per week 
Opportunities for growth and development through formal programs or mentorship 
Exclusive team member discounts and offers for more cash in your pocket, evolving policies for flexible working, leave types and access to health and wellbeing resources 

All walks, one route 

It takes a lot of us to deliver for every Australian – and it’s important to us that our people behind the parcels reflect the people receiving them. We come from all walks. Serve as the Revenue Cycle PM for the EHR Transformation program, ensuring the system design, build, testing, and deployment reflect how Fresenius Kidney Care delivers dialysis care while supporting successful adoption across approximately 2,600 clinics. Focused on partnering with Revenue cycle leadership on ensuring billing ops, financial integration, and uninterrupted charge capture, claims processing and cash collections.

Own and manage the end-to-end Revenue Cycle workstream plan, milestones, resources, and integration into the EHR program master schedule.
Lead revenue cycle design and validation activities across registration, eligibility, authorization, charge capture, coding, claims, remittance, denials, and patient collections.
Partner with Finance, Revenue Integrity, Patient Financial Services, Clinical Operations, and Information Technology teams to ensure business requirements are accurately reflected in system design and implementation plans.
Coordinate revenue cycle SMEs, analysts, operational leaders, and build teams to ensure readiness and decision closure throughout the program lifecycle.
Oversee Integrated rev cycle system configuration, including billing, payer plans, claim edits, work queues, and charge description master (CDM) integration.
Ensure readiness for all deployment waves by managing revenue protection activities including charge continuity planning, claim hold and release strategies, accounts receivable conversion, financial contingency planning, and post-go-live monitoring. Ensure dialysis-specific treatment billing processes are accurately designed and support automated charge reconciliation.
Manage third-party integrations and readiness activities with clearinghouses, payers, financial systems, and ERP platforms.
Own the revenue cycle testing strategy, including charge testing, claims testing, payer testing, remittance validation, parallel processing, and end-to-end financial testing.
Lead revenue protection and cutover planning, including charge capture continuity, claim hold/release processes, accounts receivable conversion, and first billing cycle readiness.
Monitor post-go-live financial performance metrics including charge lag, clean claim rate, denial rates, unbilled balances, and accounts receivable performance, driving issue resolution where needed.
Provide ongoing governance, risk management, status reporting, and cross-functional coordination with Clinical, Deployment, Training & Change, Finance, PMO, and ITS teams to protect revenue throughout all deployment waves.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE

Provides leadership across the Revenue Cycle Workstream consisting of Revenue Cycle Design Leads, IT Analysts, Revenue Integrity and Patient Financial Services stakeholders, Finance partners, Operational Leaders, and Vendor resources supporting the EHR Program within Care Delivery at Fresenius Medical Care. Responsible for oversight, planning, execution, and delivery of all revenue cycle activities associated with the EHR Program, including registration, coverage, eligibility, charge capture, coding, billing, claims, remittance, denials, patient collections, and financial integrations. Ensures successful implementation while protecting revenue, maintaining regulatory compliance, and supporting the financial objectives of the organization during and after EHR deployment.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

As a PM leader, provide strategic, commercially minded, entrepreneurial management leadership to the team managers, domain leads, associates and assistants.
Oversee revenue cycle design and validation efforts including patient access, registration, eligibility and authorization, charge capture, coding, billing, claims management, remittance processing, denials management, and patient collections.
Lead project management efforts across Revenue Cycle Design Leads, revenue cycle SMEs, analysts, operational stakeholders, vendor partners, and ITS resources to ensure program objectives, milestones, and deliverables are achieved.
Ensures that project management budgets and schedules are within company requirements with significant organizational responsibility for the overall control of planning, assignment of staffing, budgeting of resources, expense priority management, and recommendation and implementation changes of current methods.
Troubleshoots issues related to rev cycle project management through direct reports and with direct contact of EHR stakeholders including but not limited to sponsor clients, and FMCNA personnel.
Accountable for assisting with achieving EHR strategic direction with a focus on creating and delivering value, providing superior customer service and achieving the financial objectives for the managed cost center and for EHR in aggregate.
Strategic leader with broad-based knowledge in revenue cycle / EHR project management and rev cycle operations, and strong knowledge of industry practice and business principles. Works on complex issues and abstract issues/situations.
Leads teams including internal and external (contractor, subcontractor, vendor) staff assigned to multiple clinical workgroups
Identifies and supports new business opportunities
Ensures good working relationships with and between revenue cycle / finance / operations leaders and their staff and FMCNA personnel.
Provides oversight and assists in the recruiting and onboarding of new investigative sites as needed. Assists in the business development and business operations efforts, client relationship building activities and other sponsor facing activities as needed.
Supports the communications and negotiation of contracts related to the clinical operations while integrating input from Legal, Compliance and other entities as needed.
Direct and control the broad activities of the business unit through the interpretation, application and implementation of company­wide policies and processes appropriate to the functional area.
Works with the Compliance, Legal and Audit departments as necessary to develop or refine policies and procedures pertaining to EHR.
Review and comply with the Code of Business Conduct and all applicable company policies and procedures, local, state and federal laws and regulations.
Ensure all employees within the assigned team(s) understand and comply with the Code of Business Conduct and all applicable company policies and procedures, local, state and federal laws and regulations; establishing and maintaining effective internal systems and controls to promote compliance.
Provide leadership, guidance and coaching for all direct reports to maintain an engaged and productive workforce; partnering with Human Resources on employee matters.
Collaborate with employees in the establishment of clear and concise development plans to ensure succession planning and the advancement of future leaders within the organization.
Other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION

Required: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Health Administration, Health Information Management, or related field.
Preferred: Master's degree (MBA, MHA, or related discipline).
Preferred: PMP Certification.
Preferred: HFMA CRCR, CHFP, AHIMA, AAPC, EHR Certifications, or comparable Revenue Cycle credentials.

Experience And Required Skills

10+ years of healthcare revenue cycle, revenue cycle systems, patient financial services, or healthcare finance experience.
5+ years of project management or leadership experience.
Experience leading or supporting at least one large-scale EHR implementation involving billing conversion and production go-live.
Strong knowledge of the end-to-end healthcare revenue cycle, including registration, eligibility, authorization, charge capture, coding, claims management, remittance processing, denials, and collections.
Experience with accounts receivable conversion, payer testing, financial reconciliation, and revenue cycle stabilization following system implementations.
Understanding of Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and Commercial payer reimbursement models.
Experience working in CMS-regulated healthcare environments and knowledge of applicable reimbursement and compliance requirements.
Strong analytical skills with revenue cycle performance indicators, including charge lag, clean claim rate, denial rates, first-pass yield, days in accounts receivable, and cost-to-collect metrics.
Experience managing complex cross-functional initiatives involving Finance, Operations, IT, Clinical, and Vendor organizations.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, budgets, timelines, and stakeholder groups in large-scale transformational programs.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including executive-level presentations and financial risk communication.
Strong negotiation, influence, problem-solving, and relationship management skills.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Project, Smartsheet, Jira, ServiceNow, and reporting/analytics tools.
Dialysis, nephrology, or chronic disease management revenue cycle experience preferred.
EHR revenue cycle experience preferred.
20% to 30% travel.

jobs.title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Data
jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Program Management Team

Wayve’s Program Management team turns complex technical goals into coordinated delivery. Working closely with engineering, research and product teams, we align priorities, manage dependencies and bring clarity to ambiguous challenges. We combine technical depth with cross-functional leadership to help teams move faster, more effectively and with purpose—focusing on meaningful outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

As part of this team, you’ll build and lead the technical programme management function supporting our Data organisation. You’ll partner with Data and Engineering leadership to make valuable data immediately and reliably usable, combining hands-on ownership of flagship programmes with coaching and developing a small, high-impact TPM team.

🧠 Your day-to-day

Coach and support a small, high-impact TPM team, helping people develop their skills, work through challenges and raise the standard of programme delivery.
Act as a trusted delivery partner to Data and Engineering leadership, aligning priorities, challenging trade-offs and holding teams and leaders accountable for meaningful outcomes.
Work across data, ML, engineering and external data and annotation suppliers to manage dependencies, surface risks and remove blockers.
Use KPIs, dashboards and operational reviews to understand delivery progress, identify bottlenecks and steer decisions with the right data.
Represent the Data organisation in company-level reviews, communicating progress, risks and decisions clearly and connecting delivery to business impact.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Building and scaling the technical programme management function for our Data organisation, hiring to fill capability gaps and growing a high-performing team.
Owning planning, prioritisation and execution across the data roadmap in partnership with Data leadership.
Leading flagship programmes directly across the data platform, ingestion and standardisation pipelines, enrichment and curation, labelling and annotation, and dataset management and quality.
Establishing scalable planning cadences, governance, escalation paths and operational practices that bring structure without slowing delivery.
Driving measurable improvements in data quality, throughput, cost and time-to-insight, making the data that powers our models more reliably and predictably available.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You bring 8+ years of deep, hands-on experience delivering data programmes as a technical programme manager, spanning data platforms, pipelines, enrichment, curation or labelling. You’ve built or scaled a programme function, led people and processes, and get things done with ownership and a bias for action.
You build, coach and grow high-performing teams. You know how to develop people, hire to strengthen the team and raise the bar on technical programme management.
You have strong technical depth across data platforms, pipelines and large-scale distributed infrastructure, including platforms operating at petabyte scale. You can engage credibly with engineers without being expected to write production code. Your experience includes:
Data ingestion from raw data through multiple processing stages and pipelines, with an understanding of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), their uses and their challenges.
A solid understanding of machine learning, GPUs, and training and inference for models with 500 million to 20 billion parameters.
Proficiency with some or all of Databricks, Flyte, Ray, Kubernetes, Azure, Docker and Python.
Proficiency with AI agents such as Cursor, Claude or Codex to accelerate execution.

You stay objective under pressure and adapt your approach in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. You bring structure and clarity without creating unnecessary process or slowing delivery.
You think in systems, understanding how the parts of a complex data platform fit together and how changes in one area affect others.
You’re product-minded, focusing on the people your programmes serve, prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like—not just tracking activity.
You align and influence across data, ML and engineering without relying on formal authority.
You connect data investment to measurable outcomes, including quality, throughput and cost, and communicate direction and progress clearly using the right metrics.
You’re open to feedback and continuously improve how you and your team work.
Ideally, you’ve worked with large-scale distributed data platforms used by hundreds of engineers and researchers.
Experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics or other large-scale data and ML programmes would also be valuable.
An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer, alongside fluency with modern delivery tools such as Jira, would be a plus.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)
Competency Interviews (TPM process, Cross-functional; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (Program Design, Leadership & Management; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (30 minutes).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

We are not riding the data center wave; we are engineering it. Jacobs’ Data Center Digital Twin solution, built on NVIDIA’s Omniverse DSX Blueprint, was highlighted in Jensen Huang’s GTC keynote in March 2026, placing Jacobs at the technical frontier of gigawatt-scale AI factory design.

This is your opportunity to elevate your career to the next level — leading complex, multi-discipline programs as a Senior Project Manager (CA) Lead, across OE, EPCM, and Design-Build delivery, working alongside the most recognized hyperscale owners, colocation operators, and advanced manufacturing clients in the industry. At Jacobs, you will do what you are most passionate about, at a scale and with a client roster that defines the future of AI infrastructure. You will manage engineering-side project execution from basis of design through IFC, construction administration, commissioning, and turnover. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, manage scope, schedule, budget, fee, risk, quality, client commitments, and field coordination—while serving as the connection between design intent and site execution.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Controls

Own the project management plan scope, schedule, budget, fee forecasting, staffing, contract administration, risk register, and change controls across the delivery lifecycle.
Develop and maintain project execution plans, deliverable lists, staffing plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and client reporting; monitor progress and implement recovery actions when needed.
Manage Jacobs engineering fee budgets, subcontract scopes, cost-at-completion, variances, change orders, and commercial impacts with appropriate project-controls support.
Lead schedule development in P6, MS Project, or comparable tools; coordinate critical-path milestones across BOD, 30%/60%/IFC design, permits, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
Delivery, Construction Administration & Technical Coordination
Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams from concept through construction administration across Civil, Structural, MEP, process, controls, fire protection, and telecommunications/ICT systems, as assigned.
Serve as the primary coordination point among the client, Project Engineer, discipline design teams, construction management, commissioning teams, vendors, and subcontractors.
As Owner’s Engineer or CA lead, represent the client’s interests through design review, RFI response, submittal processing, construction observation, field issue resolution, document issuance, and schedule adherence.
Perform and coordinate field walks, engineering inspections, field checks, equipment and system verification, and line walkdowns; document observations with photos, sketches, markups, and action items.
Verify that installed conditions, equipment identification, tags, room names, system references, and drawing information are accurate, current, and traceable.
Manage RFIs, submittals, design changes, technical queries, nonconforming work, field change documentation, and potential change-order impacts through documented resolution.

Quality, Safety, Commissioning & Turnover

Enforce the Jacobs quality management plan; facilitate design QA/QC, constructability reviews, interdisciplinary coordination, and key issuance reviews at 30%/60%/IFP/IFC milestones.
Champion Jacobs BeyondZero® safety culture; review contractor safety plans and conduct site safety observations during construction-administration activities.
Support construction readiness, third-party testing, commissioning, integrated systems testing, punch-list development, system turnover, and operational handover.
Maintain complete, accurate, and auditable project records, including reports, inspection and test documentation, walkdown packages, redlines, RFIs, NCRs, meeting minutes, change logs, and closeout information.
Client Relationships & Growth
Serve as a primary client point of contact for assigned work; manage coordination meetings, dashboards, issue escalation, action closure, and executive-level communication as appropriate.
Support project staffing, onboarding, mentoring, lessons learned, continuous improvement, proposals, estimates, basis-of-estimate development, and client presentations.
Promote Jacobs’ culture of safety, quality, integrity, collaboration, and inclusion in all interactions with project teams, contractors, clients, and partners.

Here's what you'll need

Successful candidates
will possess substantial project management experience leading large-scale data center, mission-critical facility, industrial, construction, engineering, or similar physical infrastructure projects. This role is not focused on software development, enterprise IT programs, application implementation, network operations, cloud transformation, or technology product delivery. Applicants with predominantly IT Program Manager, Technical Program Manager, Software Project Manager, or SDLC-based experience should carefully review the infrastructure and construction requirements before applying.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or related discipline (or equivalent experience)
10 years or more of progressive project management, construction administration, engineering coordination, field engineering, or technical project-delivery experience on complex facilities
Demonstrated project-management or CA experience supporting Data Center, Advanced Technology, Semiconductor, mission-critical, industrial, or similarly complex facility projects; direct hyperscale experience is preferred
Fluency across at least one Jacobs delivery mode OE, EPCM, or Design-Build; ability to coordinate design, construction, commissioning, and client teams knowledge of project controls, including scheduling, cost tracking, fee forecasting, change management, risk, action tracking, and project reporting; proficiency with P6 or MS Project preferred

Preferred Qualifications

PMP (Project Management Professional) PMI certification preferred or in progress
Professional Engineer — Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, or Structural; multi-state reciprocity valued
Master’s degree in engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management
Experience on hyperscale cloud (AWS, Azure, Google, Meta) or advanced semiconductor fab (TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron) programs
LEED AP BD+C, CEA, or DBIA credential — differentiates on sustainability-driven and Design-Build pursuits
Familiarity with hyperscale design standards ASHRAE 90.4, Uptime Institute Tier classification, BICSI TDMM, NEC 708

Why Jacobs

Jacobs’ Data Center & Advanced Manufacturing practice is among the fastest-growing practices in the firm, delivering programs for hyperscale cloud providers, colocation operators, and semiconductor fab owners across the US and globally. Our portfolio includes landmark programs like the Hut 8 River Bend campus and partnerships with NVIDIA and other AI infrastructure leaders. Senior PMs at Jacobs lead programs that matter — and have direct access to a deep technical bench, a culture of innovation, and a career path that scales with the market.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has a U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $134,500.00 to $185,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 01, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. Job Description

We're looking for a Subcontract Program Manager
who will serve as the lead for an integrated set of subcontractors and matrixed-in subject matter expert support. You'll be joining a growing team to help modernize the US industrial defense.

What You'll Be Doing

Responsible for the cost, schedule and technical performance of the subcontractors and suppliers throughout program performance
Serves as the Cost Account Manager (CAM) for supply chain related expenditures to the programs; tracking proposed costs versus executed costs/quotes meticulously against performance
Bridges coordination and alignment between Technical Teams, the Program Office, and Supply Chain providing information and assistance regarding procurement programs and services; receives and responds to complaints and questions relating to assigned area of responsibility; reviews problems and recommends corrective actions
Actively engages during the proposal and business development phase to define subcontractor and supplier work that accurately capture the scale, scope and schedule of project design and delivery needs.
Analyzes risk during proposals and incorporates appropriate cost risk assessments for specific commodities or subcontracts as needed. Assists in the development of subcontract insurance, bonding and risk requirements based on subcontractor scope of work.
Works with Supply Chain and Project Management teams to compile Statements of Work (SOWs), Sole Source Justifications, Technical Evaluations, and assist in Price Analyses by providing independent estimates and make vs buy decisions as needed.
Conducts capability assessments of the supplier base and builds relationships with the supply base to aid in determining self-perform or subcontractor perform decisions
Evaluates subcontractor and supplier bids and leads or participates in source selection. Ensures selected subcontractors and suppliers are the correct fit for supply chain compliance and program execution.
Collaborates with Program Team and Supply Chain team to establish payment terms and contract types such as Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPPF), Time & Materials (T&M), etc.
Develops framework and schedules that support on time program performance that includes requisition releases plans, sounds lead time analysis and performance through to closure. Provides written and photographical documentation for all subcontractor work activities daily in documenting subcontractor progress and performance, including deficiencies associated with resources, labor productivity, equipment utilization, quality, and safety compliance consistent with the needs to document and defend change order and claims.
Assists in analyzing the Prime Contract to determine appropriate flow-down clauses
Develops a Supplier Scorecard Quarterly Business Review (QBRs) Program in partnership with Supply Chain measuring key subcontractors and suppliers on cost, schedule, quality, safety, customer responsiveness and any other key metrics as the business determines is essential for the sector’s success.
Analyzes cost / price elements in contractor proposals, bids, amendments or change orders. Regularly analyzes subcontractor and supplier costs during QBRs to ensure pricing remains in line with industry/commodity standards.
Attends/leads meetings with subcontractor partners and internal stakeholders.
Review invoices for approval based on work performed by suppliers or subcontractors.

Coordinate with the project quality assurance manager on all quality matters including those requiring their timely participation and attention to assure the project’s contract quality objectives and reporting are achieved.
Address material issues or subcontractor work problems identified by Quality Assurance by working closely with QA teams, Programs staff, and Supply Chain personnel; issue necessary notices/documentation accordingly.
Liaise with Engineering to address technical questions from supply chain, subcontractors, or suppliers
Develops process for Supply Chain related Requests for Equitable Adjustment (REAs).
Partners with Supply Chain to ensure that programs are aligned with CPSR guidelines, policies and regulations.
Stay current and knowledgeable on Parsons’ policies, Federal Acquisition Regulations and the various federal agency regulations required to maintain financial, contractual and procurement compliance.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge of principles and practices of federal contracting, FAR / DFAR supply chain management, CSPR guidelines and policies, and PMI Project Management Practices.
4-year degree in Engineering, Business, or related field, and 10 years of related work experience.
Principles, practices, and techniques of procurement and contract administration.
Principles and practices of sound financial management policies and procedures.
Strong ties with CONUS subcontractors able to execute subcontracts in excess of $20M.
Familiarity with market pricing comparable and pricing indices for merit shop labor, material, and equipment.
Organizational and management practices as applied to the analysis, evaluation, development, and implementation of programs, policies, and procedures.
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulatory codes, ordinances, and procedures relevant to assigned area of responsibility.
Modern office practices, methods, and computer equipment and applications related to the work.
English usage, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation.

Perform programmatic administrative and management activities
Conduct research on a wide variety of administrative topics including subcontracting policies, and procedures.
Analyze, interpret, summarize, and present administrative and technical information and data in an effective manner.
Research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery and improvements in operations, methods, procedures, and techniques.
Develop relationship with new subcontracting partners able to effectively support the execution of Federal construction operations.

Prepare clear and concise reports, correspondence, policies, procedures, and other written materials.
Interpret, apply, explain, and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local policies, procedures, laws, and regulations.
