new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Robotaxi
new_jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Technical Program Management Teams

The Technical Program Management team sits within Engineering Operations & Technical Program Management. Our TPMs are force multipliers, helping teams move faster, more effectively and with purpose. In Japan, you’ll be the only TPM on the ground, bridging Wayve’s global R&D with local delivery.

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Technical Program Manager for Robotaxi, you’ll own the programs that bring our robotaxi service to life, from vehicle and fleet readiness to on-the-ground launch and scaling in market. Based in Yokohama, you’ll work across autonomy, vehicle software, hardware, operations, safety and local partners to turn Wayve’s AI Driver into a safe, reliable robotaxi service, keeping complex, multi-team, cross-geography delivery predictable in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment. As the only TPM in Japan, you’ll also help support local vehicle hardware and software programs as needed.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Owning the lifecycle of robotaxi programs, from vehicle and fleet readiness to launch and in-market scaling, improving delivery through structured execution and coordination.
Tracking and managing dependencies, risks and trade-offs across autonomy, vehicle, operations and safety, and escalating early with clear options.
Keeping engineering, fleet operations, safety and local partner teams aligned, bridging Wayve’s global R&D with local delivery in Japan.
Providing hands-on program support for robotaxi launch and in-market operations, on the ground in Yokohama.
Supporting local vehicle hardware and software programs as needed, as the only TPM in Japan.
Running planning, stand-ups, reviews and retros that keep multi-team delivery predictable and reliable.
Communicating progress and risk to engineers, partners and senior leaders, tailoring updates to each audience.
Improving tooling, processes and ways of working, and sharing patterns across the TPM org.

Essential

🙌 You should apply if:

Bias for action: 5+ years leading complex, multi-team programs (or a strong record at this level). You lead high-complexity work across teams and get things done.
Technically strong across software and hardware: Credible with engineers across autonomy, vehicle software, and vehicle hardware; you reason about how the AI Driver runs as a robotaxi service on real vehicles - and can support vehicle hardware / software programs too - even though you won't write production code.
Stays neutral and adapts under pressure: Effective in ambiguous, safety-critical environments; you flex your style and bring structure without slowing delivery.
Strong project management: Skilled at planning, prioritising, and managing risk and dependencies across teams.
Exceptional communicator & collaborator: Operating from a remote office, you keep distributed teams aligned across time zones - communicating with clarity, proactively and in writing - and influence without authority across all stakeholders.
Cross-cultural & on the ground: Comfortable working across geographies and cultures, and hands-on with vehicles and operations in Japan; Japanese language skills a plus.
Generalist range: As the only TPM in-country, comfortable flexing beyond robotaxi to support vehicle hardware and software programs; happy wearing multiple hats.
Data-driven: Comfortable defining and using metrics to steer delivery and decisions.
Growth mindset: Open to feedback and always looking to improve.
Systems thinking: You reason about how the parts of a complex system fit together, and how a change in one area ripples into others.
Product-minded: You focus on outcomes and the people your programs serve - prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like, not just tracking activity.

Desirable

Robotaxi / AV operations, fleet, mobility, ride-hailing, or automotive experience; experience launching or scaling a service in market.
Exposure to ML, autonomy, or other compute-heavy / safety-critical domains; experience working across global and local teams. Japanese language skills and/or based in (or willing to relocate to) Yokohama / Tokyo.
An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency Interviews (TPM screen and technical & partnership interviews; 1 hour 45 mins total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (program design; 1 hour)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (30 mins).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

Wayve is committed to providing a fair and respectful recruitment process for all candidates, free from harassment and discrimination.

The Company has zero tolerance for sexual harassment against job applicants or similar individuals.

All communications relating to recruitment activities are conducted through the Company's recruitment system or using an email address with the Company's domain. Employees do not use their personal email addresses or social media accounts for recruitment-related communications.
Employees do not engage in private communications unrelated to recruitment activities, invite applicants to private meals, request or seek a personal or romantic relationship, or otherwise initiate private contact with applicants.
Sexual remarks or conduct, physical contact, questions concerning sexual matters, and any other conduct constituting harassment are prohibited.

If you have any concerns, you can contact our consultation desk at peoplepartners@wayve.ai. All consultations are treated with strict confidentiality, your privacy will be protected, and no one will be subject to any disadvantageous treatment for raising a concern or cooperating with an inquiry.

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

Partner with Finance, Revenue Integrity, Patient Financial Services, Clinical Operations, and Information Technology teams to ensure business requirements are accurately reflected in system design and implementation plans.
Coordinate revenue cycle SMEs, analysts, operational leaders, and build teams to ensure readiness and decision closure throughout the program lifecycle.
Oversee Integrated rev cycle system configuration, including billing, payer plans, claim edits, work queues, and charge description master (CDM) integration.
Ensure readiness for all deployment waves by managing revenue protection activities including charge continuity planning, claim hold and release strategies, accounts receivable conversion, financial contingency planning, and post-go-live monitoring. Ensure dialysis-specific treatment billing processes are accurately designed and support automated charge reconciliation.
Manage third-party integrations and readiness activities with clearinghouses, payers, financial systems, and ERP platforms.
Own the revenue cycle testing strategy, including charge testing, claims testing, payer testing, remittance validation, parallel processing, and end-to-end financial testing.
Lead revenue protection and cutover planning, including charge capture continuity, claim hold/release processes, accounts receivable conversion, and first billing cycle readiness.
Monitor post-go-live financial performance metrics including charge lag, clean claim rate, denial rates, unbilled balances, and accounts receivable performance, driving issue resolution where needed.
Provide ongoing governance, risk management, status reporting, and cross-functional coordination with Clinical, Deployment, Training & Change, Finance, PMO, and ITS teams to protect revenue throughout all deployment waves.

new_jobs.title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Data
new_jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Program Management Team

Wayve’s Program Management team turns complex technical goals into coordinated delivery. Working closely with engineering, research and product teams, we align priorities, manage dependencies and bring clarity to ambiguous challenges. We combine technical depth with cross-functional leadership to help teams move faster, more effectively and with purpose—focusing on meaningful outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

As part of this team, you’ll build and lead the technical programme management function supporting our Data organisation. You’ll partner with Data and Engineering leadership to make valuable data immediately and reliably usable, combining hands-on ownership of flagship programmes with coaching and developing a small, high-impact TPM team.

🧠 Your day-to-day

Coach and support a small, high-impact TPM team, helping people develop their skills, work through challenges and raise the standard of programme delivery.
Act as a trusted delivery partner to Data and Engineering leadership, aligning priorities, challenging trade-offs and holding teams and leaders accountable for meaningful outcomes.
Work across data, ML, engineering and external data and annotation suppliers to manage dependencies, surface risks and remove blockers.
Use KPIs, dashboards and operational reviews to understand delivery progress, identify bottlenecks and steer decisions with the right data.
Represent the Data organisation in company-level reviews, communicating progress, risks and decisions clearly and connecting delivery to business impact.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Building and scaling the technical programme management function for our Data organisation, hiring to fill capability gaps and growing a high-performing team.
Owning planning, prioritisation and execution across the data roadmap in partnership with Data leadership.
Leading flagship programmes directly across the data platform, ingestion and standardisation pipelines, enrichment and curation, labelling and annotation, and dataset management and quality.
Establishing scalable planning cadences, governance, escalation paths and operational practices that bring structure without slowing delivery.
Driving measurable improvements in data quality, throughput, cost and time-to-insight, making the data that powers our models more reliably and predictably available.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You bring 8+ years of deep, hands-on experience delivering data programmes as a technical programme manager, spanning data platforms, pipelines, enrichment, curation or labelling. You’ve built or scaled a programme function, led people and processes, and get things done with ownership and a bias for action.
You build, coach and grow high-performing teams. You know how to develop people, hire to strengthen the team and raise the bar on technical programme management.
You have strong technical depth across data platforms, pipelines and large-scale distributed infrastructure, including platforms operating at petabyte scale. You can engage credibly with engineers without being expected to write production code. Your experience includes:
Data ingestion from raw data through multiple processing stages and pipelines, with an understanding of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), their uses and their challenges.
A solid understanding of machine learning, GPUs, and training and inference for models with 500 million to 20 billion parameters.
Proficiency with some or all of Databricks, Flyte, Ray, Kubernetes, Azure, Docker and Python.
Proficiency with AI agents such as Cursor, Claude or Codex to accelerate execution.

You stay objective under pressure and adapt your approach in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. You bring structure and clarity without creating unnecessary process or slowing delivery.
You think in systems, understanding how the parts of a complex data platform fit together and how changes in one area affect others.
You’re product-minded, focusing on the people your programmes serve, prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like—not just tracking activity.
You align and influence across data, ML and engineering without relying on formal authority.
You connect data investment to measurable outcomes, including quality, throughput and cost, and communicate direction and progress clearly using the right metrics.
You’re open to feedback and continuously improve how you and your team work.
Ideally, you’ve worked with large-scale distributed data platforms used by hundreds of engineers and researchers.
Experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics or other large-scale data and ML programmes would also be valuable.
An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer, alongside fluency with modern delivery tools such as Jira, would be a plus.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)
Competency Interviews (TPM process, Cross-functional; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (Program Design, Leadership & Management; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (30 minutes).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

Work across ML and research, infrastructure, embedded and on-vehicle engineering teams, as well as cloud and vendor partners, to manage dependencies, surface risks and remove blockers.
Use KPIs, dashboards and operational reviews to understand delivery progress, identify bottlenecks and steer decisions with the right data.
Represent AI Platform in company-level reviews, communicating progress, risks and decisions clearly while connecting delivery to business impact.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Building and scaling the technical programme management function for AI Platform, hiring to fill capability gaps and growing a high-performing team.
Owning planning, prioritisation and execution across the AI Platform roadmap in partnership with engineering leadership.
Leading flagship programmes across data and compute infrastructure, developer tooling, training technology, compute management, model-development workflows, and embedded and inference optimisation.
Establishing scalable planning cadences, governance, escalation paths and operational practices that bring structure without slowing delivery.
Driving measurable improvements in developer velocity, compute efficiency and cost, training and inference performance, and platform reliability.
Helping engineering leaders deliver high-leverage outcomes, balancing technical trade-offs and ensuring commitments translate into impact.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You bring 8+ years of hands-on technical programme management experience across platform, infrastructure, compute, ML infrastructure, developer tooling, training or inference systems. You have built or scaled a programme function, led people and processes, and get things done with ownership and a bias for action.
You build, coach and grow high-performing teams. You know how to develop people, hire to strengthen the team and raise the bar on technical programme management.
You have strong technical depth across ML infrastructure, compute and embedded systems. You can engage credibly with platform and systems engineers without being expected to write production code. Your experience includes:
A strong understanding of machine learning, GPUs, and training and inference for models from 500M to 20B+ parameters, including the compute and orchestration that support them.
Embedded or on-vehicle systems experience, including inference optimisation, deploying models to constrained edge compute, and hardware-software trade-offs.
Familiarity with compute management, ML platform tooling and model-development or experiment workflows, using technologies such as Kubernetes, Ray, Flyte, Docker, Azure and Python.
Proficiency with AI agents and coding assistants such as Cursor, Claude or Codex to accelerate execution.

You stay objective under pressure and adapt your approach in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. You bring structure and clarity without creating unnecessary process or slowing delivery.
You think in systems, understanding how the parts of a complex platform stack fit together and how changes in one area affect others.
You’re product-minded, focusing on the people your programmes serve, prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like—not just tracking activity.
You align and influence across ML and research, infrastructure, embedded and engineering teams without relying on formal authority.
You connect technical investment to measurable outcomes, including developer velocity, compute efficiency, cost and model performance, and communicate direction and progress clearly using the right metrics.
You’re open to feedback and continuously improve how you and your team work.
Ideally, you have worked with a large-scale ML or compute platform used by hundreds of engineers and researchers.
Experience with embedded or edge inference, on-device model optimisation, hardware-aware ML, autonomous vehicles, robotics or another large-scale ML and infrastructure environment would be valuable.
An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer, would be a plus.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)
Competency Interviews (TPM process, Cross-functional; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (Program Design, Leadership & Management; 1 hour 45 minutes total)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (30 minutes).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

new_jobs.title: Sr Project Manager - AI Data Centers
new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

This job opportunity is available at ANY location in the United States. Ideally, selected candidates will be near a JACOBS U.S. based office, but we intend to hire the "best" candidates.

Your impact

Jacobs is the #1-ranked design firm on ENR’s Top 500 Design Firms list — for the seventh consecutive year — and the #1 Program Management firm globally (ENR, 2025). We are not riding the data center wave; we are engineering it. Jacobs’ Data Center Digital Twin solution, built on NVIDIA’s Omniverse DSX Blueprint, was highlighted in Jensen Huang’s GTC keynote in March 2026, placing Jacobs at the technical frontier of gigawatt-scale AI factory design.

This is your opportunity to elevate your career to the next level — leading complex, multi-discipline programs as a Senior Project Manager (CA) Lead, across OE, EPCM, and Design-Build delivery, working alongside the most recognized hyperscale owners, colocation operators, and advanced manufacturing clients in the industry. At Jacobs, you will do what you are most passionate about, at a scale and with a client roster that defines the future of AI infrastructure. You will manage engineering-side project execution from basis of design through IFC, construction administration, commissioning, and turnover. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, manage scope, schedule, budget, fee, risk, quality, client commitments, and field coordination—while serving as the connection between design intent and site execution.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Controls

Own the project management plan scope, schedule, budget, fee forecasting, staffing, contract administration, risk register, and change controls across the delivery lifecycle.
Develop and maintain project execution plans, deliverable lists, staffing plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and client reporting; monitor progress and implement recovery actions when needed.
Manage Jacobs engineering fee budgets, subcontract scopes, cost-at-completion, variances, change orders, and commercial impacts with appropriate project-controls support.
Lead schedule development in P6, MS Project, or comparable tools; coordinate critical-path milestones across BOD, 30%/60%/IFC design, permits, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
Delivery, Construction Administration & Technical Coordination
Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams from concept through construction administration across Civil, Structural, MEP, process, controls, fire protection, and telecommunications/ICT systems, as assigned.
Serve as the primary coordination point among the client, Project Engineer, discipline design teams, construction management, commissioning teams, vendors, and subcontractors.
As Owner’s Engineer or CA lead, represent the client’s interests through design review, RFI response, submittal processing, construction observation, field issue resolution, document issuance, and schedule adherence.
Perform and coordinate field walks, engineering inspections, field checks, equipment and system verification, and line walkdowns; document observations with photos, sketches, markups, and action items.
Verify that installed conditions, equipment identification, tags, room names, system references, and drawing information are accurate, current, and traceable.
Manage RFIs, submittals, design changes, technical queries, nonconforming work, field change documentation, and potential change-order impacts through documented resolution.

Quality, Safety, Commissioning & Turnover

Enforce the Jacobs quality management plan; facilitate design QA/QC, constructability reviews, interdisciplinary coordination, and key issuance reviews at 30%/60%/IFP/IFC milestones.
Champion Jacobs BeyondZero® safety culture; review contractor safety plans and conduct site safety observations during construction-administration activities.
Support construction readiness, third-party testing, commissioning, integrated systems testing, punch-list development, system turnover, and operational handover.
Maintain complete, accurate, and auditable project records, including reports, inspection and test documentation, walkdown packages, redlines, RFIs, NCRs, meeting minutes, change logs, and closeout information.
Client Relationships & Growth
Serve as a primary client point of contact for assigned work; manage coordination meetings, dashboards, issue escalation, action closure, and executive-level communication as appropriate.
Support project staffing, onboarding, mentoring, lessons learned, continuous improvement, proposals, estimates, basis-of-estimate development, and client presentations.
Promote Jacobs’ culture of safety, quality, integrity, collaboration, and inclusion in all interactions with project teams, contractors, clients, and partners.

Here's what you'll need

Successful candidates
will possess substantial project management experience leading large-scale data center, mission-critical facility, industrial, construction, engineering, or similar physical infrastructure projects. This role is not focused on software development, enterprise IT programs, application implementation, network operations, cloud transformation, or technology product delivery. Applicants with predominantly IT Program Manager, Technical Program Manager, Software Project Manager, or SDLC-based experience should carefully review the infrastructure and construction requirements before applying.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or related discipline (or equivalent experience)
10 years or more of progressive project management, construction administration, engineering coordination, field engineering, or technical project-delivery experience on complex facilities
Demonstrated project-management or CA experience supporting Data Center, Advanced Technology, Semiconductor, mission-critical, industrial, or similarly complex facility projects; direct hyperscale experience is preferred
Fluency across at least one Jacobs delivery mode OE, EPCM, or Design-Build; ability to coordinate design, construction, commissioning, and client teams knowledge of project controls, including scheduling, cost tracking, fee forecasting, change management, risk, action tracking, and project reporting; proficiency with P6 or MS Project preferred

Preferred Qualifications

PMP (Project Management Professional) PMI certification preferred or in progress
Professional Engineer — Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, or Structural; multi-state reciprocity valued
Master’s degree in engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management
Experience on hyperscale cloud (AWS, Azure, Google, Meta) or advanced semiconductor fab (TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron) programs
LEED AP BD+C, CEA, or DBIA credential — differentiates on sustainability-driven and Design-Build pursuits
Familiarity with hyperscale design standards ASHRAE 90.4, Uptime Institute Tier classification, BICSI TDMM, NEC 708

Why Jacobs

Jacobs’ Data Center & Advanced Manufacturing practice is among the fastest-growing practices in the firm, delivering programs for hyperscale cloud providers, colocation operators, and semiconductor fab owners across the US and globally. Our portfolio includes landmark programs like the Hut 8 River Bend campus and partnerships with NVIDIA and other AI infrastructure leaders. Senior PMs at Jacobs lead programs that matter — and have direct access to a deep technical bench, a culture of innovation, and a career path that scales with the market.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has a U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $134,500.00 to $185,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 01, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

In this role, you'll:

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

We're looking for a Subcontract Program Manager
who will serve as the lead for an integrated set of subcontractors and matrixed-in subject matter expert support. You'll be joining a growing team to help modernize the US industrial defense.

What You'll Be Doing

Responsible for the cost, schedule and technical performance of the subcontractors and suppliers throughout program performance
Serves as the Cost Account Manager (CAM) for supply chain related expenditures to the programs; tracking proposed costs versus executed costs/quotes meticulously against performance
Bridges coordination and alignment between Technical Teams, the Program Office, and Supply Chain providing information and assistance regarding procurement programs and services; receives and responds to complaints and questions relating to assigned area of responsibility; reviews problems and recommends corrective actions
Actively engages during the proposal and business development phase to define subcontractor and supplier work that accurately capture the scale, scope and schedule of project design and delivery needs.
Analyzes risk during proposals and incorporates appropriate cost risk assessments for specific commodities or subcontracts as needed. Assists in the development of subcontract insurance, bonding and risk requirements based on subcontractor scope of work.
Works with Supply Chain and Project Management teams to compile Statements of Work (SOWs), Sole Source Justifications, Technical Evaluations, and assist in Price Analyses by providing independent estimates and make vs buy decisions as needed.
Conducts capability assessments of the supplier base and builds relationships with the supply base to aid in determining self-perform or subcontractor perform decisions
Evaluates subcontractor and supplier bids and leads or participates in source selection. Ensures selected subcontractors and suppliers are the correct fit for supply chain compliance and program execution.
Collaborates with Program Team and Supply Chain team to establish payment terms and contract types such as Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPPF), Time & Materials (T&M), etc.
Develops framework and schedules that support on time program performance that includes requisition releases plans, sounds lead time analysis and performance through to closure. Coordinates with assigned Subcontracts Administrator and Buyer to release RFPs and gather appropriate documentation from the program team to ensure compliance and agile teamwork.
Maintains accurate records and files; develops storage of records for program and technical updates, schedules, SDRLs, and other deliverables. Works with Supply Chain to ensure suppliers are maintaining contractual compliance throughout period of performance.
Provides written and photographical documentation for all subcontractor work activities daily in documenting subcontractor progress and performance, including deficiencies associated with resources, labor productivity, equipment utilization, quality, and safety compliance consistent with the needs to document and defend change order and claims.
Assists in analyzing the Prime Contract to determine appropriate flow-down clauses
Develops a Supplier Scorecard Quarterly Business Review (QBRs) Program in partnership with Supply Chain measuring key subcontractors and suppliers on cost, schedule, quality, safety, customer responsiveness and any other key metrics as the business determines is essential for the sector’s success.
Analyzes cost / price elements in contractor proposals, bids, amendments or change orders. Regularly analyzes subcontractor and supplier costs during QBRs to ensure pricing remains in line with industry/commodity standards.
Attends/leads meetings with subcontractor partners and internal stakeholders.
Review invoices for approval based on work performed by suppliers or subcontractors.
Provide oversight of subcontractors/supplier’ compliance to their quality control plan, including inspection requirements and reporting. Work and communicate effectively with onsite customer representatives to assure a continuous and uninterrupted workflow. Coordinate with the project quality assurance manager on all quality matters including those requiring their timely participation and attention to assure the project’s contract quality objectives and reporting are achieved.
Address material issues or subcontractor work problems identified by Quality Assurance by working closely with QA teams, Programs staff, and Supply Chain personnel; issue necessary notices/documentation accordingly.
Liaise with Engineering to address technical questions from supply chain, subcontractors, or suppliers
Develops process for Supply Chain related Requests for Equitable Adjustment (REAs).
Partners with Supply Chain to ensure that programs are aligned with CPSR guidelines, policies and regulations.
Stay current and knowledgeable on Parsons’ policies, Federal Acquisition Regulations and the various federal agency regulations required to maintain financial, contractual and procurement compliance.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge of principles and practices of federal contracting, FAR / DFAR supply chain management, CSPR guidelines and policies, and PMI Project Management Practices.
4-year degree in Engineering, Business, or related field, and 10 years of related work experience.
Principles, practices, and techniques of procurement and contract administration.
Principles and practices of sound financial management policies and procedures.
Strong ties with CONUS subcontractors able to execute subcontracts in excess of $20M.
Familiarity with market pricing comparable and pricing indices for merit shop labor, material, and equipment.
Organizational and management practices as applied to the analysis, evaluation, development, and implementation of programs, policies, and procedures.
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulatory codes, ordinances, and procedures relevant to assigned area of responsibility.
Modern office practices, methods, and computer equipment and applications related to the work.
English usage, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation.

What Desired Skills You'll Bring

Perform programmatic administrative and management activities
Conduct research on a wide variety of administrative topics including subcontracting policies, and procedures.
Analyze, interpret, summarize, and present administrative and technical information and data in an effective manner.
Research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery and improvements in operations, methods, procedures, and techniques.
Develop relationship with new subcontracting partners able to effectively support the execution of Federal construction operations.
Travel for meetings with internal team members and external subcontractors, not anticipated to exceed 2 trips per month.
Prepare clear and concise reports, correspondence, policies, procedures, and other written materials.
Interpret, apply, explain, and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local policies, procedures, laws, and regulations.
Effectively representing Parsons in contacts with governmental agencies, community groups, and various business, professional, educational, regulatory, and legislative organizations.
Establish and maintain a variety of filing, record keeping, and tracking systems.
Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner; organize own work, set priorities, and meet critical time deadlines.
Operate and maintain modern office equipment, including computer equipment and specialized software applications programs.
Effectively communicate in-person, over the telephone, and in writing.
Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy and legal guidelines in politically sensitive situations.
Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

The role will be based in any Forestry England office preferably within the Midlands, with flexibility for blended working (with the ability to commute to the local Forestry England office regularly).

There will be a need for travel in this role, with occasional overnight stays necessary.

Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas.

Benefits…

Alongside your salary, Forestry England contributes an average of 28.97% towards your pension. You will become a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension Scheme.

Other Benefits Include

25 days holiday a year, raising by one day every year’s service, up to 30 days (pro-rated for part time employees) plus additional days off such as bank holidays.
STaR is our employee benefits scheme offering discounts on everyday supermarket shopping, as well as other things such as hotel stays clothes, mobile phones, other electrical items, medical and car insurance, holidays, gym discounts, household bills, Headspace wellbeing app.
free parking at Forestry England sites and free entry to our National Arboretums at Westonbirt and Bedgebury.
a commitment to lifelong learning through career development. Forestry England will support your career development in a variety of ways, including continual professional development, support for individual learning plans and sponsored membership of professional bodies.

Read more about the benefits on the Forestry England website.

How To Apply…

We cannot accept applications via email. Please follow the steps outlined below. Any CVs and/or personal statements sent outside the system will not be considered for shortlisting.

You will be asked to write a 200 word statement on your relevant experience and career history, along with a personal statement of no more than 500 words. You will be assessed on both during sifting. More details about how to apply are listed on the application form.

The selection process may include additional assessment and/or interview stages. Candidates will be informed of the assessment format and arrangements during the recruitment process.

The Behaviours being assessed at interview are –

Communicating and Influencing
Changing and Improving
Working together
Managing a Quality Service

You may also be assessed on Experience, Strength based questions, and/or the Technical Success Profile at the interview. The technical element could include a presentation, practical or written task.

If candidates pass the interview but are not the leading candidate, they can be placed on a reserve list. We may offer candidates on the reserve list for this role the opportunity to be considered for other roles at the same or lower pay bands.

Internal: Please note that if you are an internal candidate on a permanent contract and you apply for a Fixed Term Appointment of three years or more, your substantive role will not be held open. You will retain your permanent status. At the end of the FTA, HR and your new Cost Centre Manager will attempt to find you a suitable alternative post in line with the Redeployment policy. If no suitable alternative post can be found, you will be managed under Redundancy policy.

If you move to a post in a higher pay band through fair and open competition for a period of less than three years, then you will be considered to be on a period of ‘temporary promotion’, if three years or more then you will be considered to be permanently promoted .

Successful candidates will undergo a criminal record check and the government baseline personnel security standard check.

If you require any reasonable adjustments, please email fcrecruitmentteam@forestryengland.uk.

If you're planning to use AI to support your application, please ensure you've read our guidelines here first.

Read more about our application process and working with us on the Forestry England website.

Nationality Requirements…

Read more about nationality requirements for working in the Civil Service on GOV.UK.

Working for the Civil Service…

Forestry England is part of the Civil Service. The Civil Service has a Disability Confident Scheme (DCS). This means candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum selection criteria during the application process will be guaranteed an interview. We also offer a Redeployment Interview Scheme to current civil servants who are at risk of redundancy, and who meet the minimum requirements for the role. This role is also part of the Great Place to Work for Veterans and Prison Leaver Recruitment initiative.

This role is funded by DEFRA rather than through Forestry England generated revenue and is therefore subject to government spending reviews. While DEFRA has indicated long term support for the Biodiversity Programme and we expect funding to continue, it is possible that funding levels may change at the end of any financial year depending on DEFRA’s budget allocations. In the event of funding changes, we would prioritise retaining staff posts wherever possible. This approach is consistent for roles within publicly funded organisations. We are committed to keeping staff informed and supported through any changes.

Within Part 7 of the Immigration Act 2016, it is essential that applicants should have the ability to provide conversation in accurate spoken English.

Our recruitment process makes appointments based on fair and open competition and merit, as outlined in the Civil Service Commissioners’ Recruitment Principles. Le/la Chef de projet Construction et Mise en service (PMCC) est responsable de la préparation et du contrôle des différentes phases des opérations sur site pour un projet. Ce rôle est essentiel pour garantir que les travaux sur site sont réalisés en toute sécurité, selon les standards de qualité requis, dans les délais et dans le respect du budget. Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) possède une vaste expérience en gestion de chantiers, de solides compétences en gestion et la capacité de résoudre les problèmes rapidement et efficacement.

Responsabilités Principales

Participer à la définition de la stratégie des travaux sur site avec le Directeur de Projet, le Responsable de Construction et le Chef de Chantier
Anticiper de manière proactive les activités nécessaires à la mobilisation du site, y compris la définition des outillages, des équipements de sécurité, des besoins en stockage, des infrastructures de bureaux, des logements pour les travailleurs, et définir les formations spécifiques requises sur site

Réaliser des analyses financières détaillées incluant, sans s’y limiter, l’établissement des budgets, le suivi des coûts engagés, les dérives, les réclamations et les prévisions
S’impliquer de manière proactive dans la mitigation des risques et l’évaluation des opportunités
Se déplacer sur les sites environ 25 % du temps pour examiner et soutenir les opérations sur site
Réaliser la mise à jour hebdomadaire du planning de chantier (prévu vs réalisé) en collaboration avec le chef de site et le planificateur de projet
Coordonner les communications entre les équipes projet afin de sécuriser la planification et l’exécution du projet
Participer aux réunions interne et avec le client
Identifier les évolutions de périmètre pour les travaux sur site et superviser les parties prenantes pour en évaluer les impacts en quantité et en qualité
Préparer les demandes de devis et les demandes d’achat pour la sous-traitance des travaux sur site

Préparer et piloter la démobilisation du site en fin de projet

Forte culture Environnement, Santé, et Sécurité
Sens aigu de la gestion de la qualité et engagement envers l’amélioration continue de la culture qualité
Solide expérience dans le domaine de l’hydroélectricité

Expérience en gestion de chantier est un atout
Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale (anglais et français)
Compétences en leadership
Disponibilité pour voyager à travers le Canada
Plus de 10 ans d’expérience dans une organisation de gestion de projets en Construction ou Mise en service, ou 3 à 5 ans d’expérience directe

Certification en gestion de projet
Expérience avec des concepts techniques (incluant la technologie hydroélectrique, par ex. turbines, alternateurs, systèmes de balance of plant mécaniques et électriques, etc.)

Excellent communication skills written and verbal (English and French)

new_jobs.title: Security Operations Analyst (L1) – MS- Defender
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Security Operations Analyst (L1) – MS Defender based in India.

As a Security Operations Analyst, you will play an important role in protecting enterprise IT environments through continuous security monitoring and first-level incident response. You will be responsible for monitoring Microsoft Defender security alerts, identifying suspicious activities, and performing initial investigations to help detect potential threats. Working within a global security operations environment, you will support endpoint protection, validate device security status, and ensure incidents are properly documented and escalated. You will collaborate with SOC specialists, infrastructure teams, and senior security analysts to support effective threat detection and response. By following established security procedures and operational runbooks, you will contribute to maintaining a strong security posture across enterprise environments. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your cybersecurity expertise in a collaborative, fast-paced, and continuously evolving technical environment.

Accountabilities

Monitor Microsoft Defender: Continuously monitor Microsoft Defender portals, security dashboards, alert queues, and incident notifications to identify potential security threats and endpoint protection issues.
Perform initial alert triage: Review malware detections, suspicious activities, and endpoint security alerts, assessing device information, severity levels, timestamps, and potential business impact.
Validate endpoint protection: Perform basic checks on Defender sensor health, endpoint onboarding status, protection configurations, and security coverage.
Identify security vulnerabilities and issues: Detect endpoints with failed scans, outdated security intelligence, inactive sensors, or other protection-related problems and report them through established procedures.
Escalate potential threats: Identify suspicious activities and high-severity alerts and escalate them promptly to L2/L3 analysts and relevant security teams according to established escalation procedures.
Manage security incidents: Create, categorize, prioritize, and update incident tickets using ServiceNow or equivalent IT Service Management platforms.
Collect investigation evidence: Gather and document relevant alert information, device details, timestamps, and initial investigation findings to support further analysis.
Execute security runbooks: Perform approved first-level investigation and validation activities by following documented security procedures and operational guidelines.
Coordinate incident resolution: Track open incidents and collaborate with L2/L3 analysts, SOC teams, and endpoint specialists throughout investigation and remediation activities.
Validate remediation activities: Confirm endpoint protection recovery and remediation status as instructed by senior security teams, ensuring incidents are accurately updated.
Follow security procedures: Respect established authorization boundaries and escalation protocols, avoiding unauthorized containment or remediation actions.
Maintain operational compliance: Follow security incident management, incident, change, and service request processes while ensuring timely alert acknowledgement and SLA compliance.
Document operational activities: Maintain accurate incident records, operational checklists, investigation notes, and shift handover documentation.
Collaborate across teams: Coordinate with SOC, Endpoint, Identity, Infrastructure, and L2/L3 teams to support effective security operations.
Support reporting and improvement: Contribute to routine security reports, alert tracking, and operational reviews while identifying recurring alerts and reporting monitoring or documentation gaps.
Ensure global monitoring continuity: Facilitate effective handovers across APAC, EMEA, and North America teams to maintain uninterrupted 24/7 security monitoring.

Requirements

Professional experience: 1–3 years of experience in IT operations, security monitoring, endpoint support, or security incident management.
Endpoint security knowledge: Basic understanding of endpoint protection technologies, antivirus solutions, malware detection, and common security alerts.
Microsoft Defender expertise: Familiarity with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint or equivalent endpoint protection platforms. Practical experience with Microsoft Defender is highly desirable.
Windows operating systems: Basic knowledge of Windows environments, system processes, endpoint health, and troubleshooting fundamentals.
Security alert investigation: Ability to review security alerts, identify relevant information, collect evidence, and follow documented investigation procedures.
Incident management: Understanding of incident severity levels, escalation matrices, response procedures, and SLA requirements.
ITSM tools: Familiarity with ServiceNow or equivalent IT Service Management platforms for incident logging, tracking, and documentation.
Communication skills: Good written and verbal communication abilities, with the capacity to provide clear investigation updates and accurate shift handovers.
Documentation and organization: Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate incident records while following established security procedures.
Shift flexibility: Willingness to work rotational shifts in a 24/7 security operations environment, supporting global teams and continuous monitoring.
Security certifications: Microsoft SC-900 or an equivalent security fundamentals certification is an advantage.
Extended security knowledge: Basic familiarity with Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel is desirable.
Threat awareness: Understanding of malware, phishing, endpoint threats, and common cyberattack techniques is beneficial.
Scripting and troubleshooting: Basic knowledge of PowerShell and Windows troubleshooting is a plus.
Security analytics: Exposure to Kusto Query Language (KQL), security dashboards, alert analysis, and incident reporting is desirable.
ITIL knowledge: Familiarity with ITIL principles and security incident management processes is an advantage.
Key competencies: Knowledge of security monitoring, Microsoft Defender, alert triage, endpoint protection, basic threat analysis, evidence collection, runbook execution, incident logging, escalation management, SLA compliance, and global 24/7 operations.

Benefits

Professional development: Opportunities to develop expertise in cybersecurity, endpoint protection, and enterprise security operations.

new_jobs.title: TPO Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Description

POSITION OVERVIEW:

We are looking for a TPO Business Analyst to join our TPO Business Strategy team to serve as the analytical engine connecting product development, operations, and enterprise partner feedback. This role will own product and process gap analysis — identifying where our TPO platform falls short against enterprise partner needs, investor requirements, and operational best practices — and translate those findings into actionable requirements for engineering and process improvements for operations. The ideal candidate will have experience in solar finance, business analysis, or operations and will work across Product, Engineering, Operations, Capital Markets, and Risk teams.  

This position will be based out of San Francisco, CA or Santa Clara, CA with an in-office schedule set at the direct manager’s discretion in accordance with the company policies and procedures. 

Responsibilities

Conduct end-to-end product and process gap analyses by mapping the TPO customer journey (sale creation through asset onboarding), identifying structural gaps, and categorizing them by severity and business impact — similar in scope to internal initiatives like Project Clarity.  
Translate voice-of-customer feedback from enterprise installer partners and investor/capital markets stakeholders into structured product requirements and operational process change proposals for Engineering and Operations teams.  
Own change order and milestone enforcement analysis — evaluate current process controls (e.g., CO enforcement at NTP, M2 as-built verification, Year 1 kWh reconciliation), identify attack vectors and failure modes, and design minimum viable fixes that require no or minimal engineering development.  
Build detailed gap analysis deliverables (Word docs, Excel models, process flow diagrams) that clearly articulate current state vs. target state, root cause, and prioritized remediation paths with implementation timelines. 
Partner with the Operations team to redesign operational process flows when gaps are identified — drafting new SOPs, updating milestone checklists, and coordinating rollout across QSS and internal ops stakeholders.  
Support product development prioritization by maintaining a living backlog of product gaps mapped to partner impact, investor risk, and revenue exposure — enabling data-driven sprint planning conversations with Engineering.  
Analyze PI (Partner Installer) behavior patterns using Salesforce data to identify systemic risks such as production overstatement, CO circumvention, and documentation non-compliance, and recommend systemic controls.  
Participate in cross-functional project meetings (e.g., CLS issue mapping, PMO-led initiatives) and produce structured meeting notes, action item trackers, and follow-up deliverables.   

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, finance, economics, engineering, data analytics, or a related field with a minimum of 5+ years of professional work experience in business analysis, operations analysis, management consulting, or strategy/operations role in solar finance, fintech, or financial services. 
Strong analytical skills with the ability to map complex multi-step processes, identify failure points, and propose structured solutions — comfort with process flow mapping and root cause analysis. 
Proficiency in Excel (financial modeling, data analysis) and PowerPoint (structured presentations for leadership audiences). 
Excellent written communication — ability to produce clear, structured gap analysis documents, SOPs, and requirements specifications. 
Comfort working across multiple teams simultaneously (Product, Engineering, Operations, Capital Markets) in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in residential solar TPO operations, loan servicing, or asset management — familiarity with milestone-based workflows (NTP, M1, M2, M3). 
Familiarity with Salesforce as a system of record and experience pulling operational data for analysis. 
Exposure to investor reporting, capital markets due diligence, or portfolio quality analysis in a renewable energy or structured finance context. 
Experience with process improvement frameworks (Lean, Six Sigma) or project management tools (Jira, Asana, Miro). 
SQL or BI tool experience (Tableau, Looker) for operational data analysis is a plus. 

WHY QCELLS?:

This is an opportunity to lead an end-to-end North American BESS business and shape its strategy, growth, product portfolio, commercial model, supply chain, and execution platform.

The role offers direct executive visibility with Qcells and Hanwha leadership and the opportunity to build a scalable BESS organization across the North American market.

Qcells is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Compensation

In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws, the anticipated annual base salary for this position is:

Zone 1 (Bay Area, NYC): $120,400 – $144,400
Zone 2 (CA, NJ, NY): $110,300 – $132,300
Zone 3 (All others): $100,300 – $120,300

The applicable salary range is based on the employee’s primary work location. Individual compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, education, skills, internal equity, and other business-related factors.

Hanwha Q CELLS America Inc. (“HQCA”) is a Qcells company, one of the world’s largest manufacturers and providers of solar photovoltaic (PV) products and solutions.  Headquartered in Irvine, California, HQCA has been rapidly expanding its business in North America through the expansion of products and solutions, including distributed energy solutions, direct-to-homeowner solar sales and financing, and EPC services.  We provide an opportunity to be part of an exciting and growing world-class global business in an interesting and expanding industry of the future.

This position requires the ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. Periodic travel and site visits may be required.

The salary range is required by the California Pay Transparency Act and may differ depending on the location of those candidates hired nationwide. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to, skill set, education, licenses and certifications, essential job duties and requirements, and the necessary experience relative to the job’s minimum qualifications.

This target salary range is for CA positions only and should not be interpreted as an offer of compensation.

new_jobs.description:
About The Position

Ready to turn data into insights that help power the future of energy? As an Associate Data Analyst, you'll use data to uncover trends, solve business challenges, and help drive smarter decisions across major electric infrastructure projects. Working with financial, project, and operational data, you'll transform complex information into meaningful insights that support the estimating team and contribute to the delivery of critical investments that keep communities connected.

In this role, you'll collaborate with estimators and stakeholders across the business to analyze data, build dashboards, create impactful reports, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency. You'll develop experience with data visualization, analytics, and emerging technologies while strengthening your technical, business, and communication skills. If you're naturally curious, enjoy solving problems, and want to see the real-world impact of your work, you'll thrive on this collaborative team that values fresh ideas, continuous learning, and innovation.

What You’ll Do

Analyze financial, project, and operational data to uncover trends, answer business questions, and support decision-making across capital electric projects.
Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and visualizations that help stakeholders turn data into actionable insights.
Partner with estimators and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency, and streamline workflows.
Support data extraction, validation, and reporting activities to help ensure information is accurate, reliable, and meaningful.
Present findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences, translating complex data into clear takeaways.
Explore emerging analytics, automation, and AI tools while developing your technical, business, and problem-solving skills through real-world projects and collaboration.

What You'll Need to Apply

Bachelors or Master's degree from an accredited institution. Preferably in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Finance, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics or a related field.
Problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate data, identify trends, and support business decisions.
Ability to communicate insights clearly and collaborate effectively with a variety of stakeholders.
Graduated between May 2026 and June 2027
Ability to begin the National Grid Graduate Program on June 7, 2027, or July 12, 2027
Valid driver’s license required with a safe driving history that meets National Grid’s Safe Driver policy
Work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States (such as sponsorship for an H-1B, TN, O, L, STEM OPT, or other employment-based work authorization)

It would be awesome if you had

Experience using tools like Python, SQL, Snowflake, or similar technologies to explore data, solve problems, and uncover insights.
Experience creating dashboards, reports, or data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or other reporting tools.
Demonstrated leadership, teamwork, or stakeholder engagement through student organizations, academic projects, internships, volunteer work, athletics, or extracurricular activities.

What You’ll Get in Return

Structured development opportunities, mentorship, and ongoing feedback to accelerate your career growth
Exposure to leaders, cross-functional teams, and diverse areas of the business
Opportunities to build your professional network and develop lasting industry connections
Meaningful work and real-world experience that provide a strong foundation for a long-term career at National Grid
Competitive salary ranging from $73,000 to $86,000, plus a comprehensive benefits package
Financial support for your future through up to $6,000 in student loan repayment assistance and tuition reimbursement benefits of up to $8,000 annually for undergraduate studies and $10,000 annually for graduate studies

About The Graduate Development Program

National Grid’s Graduate Development Program (GDP) is a year-long development program for recent college graduates who aspire to take on future leadership roles in a dynamic, ever-changing industry. Graduates will shape the future of National Grid. Bringing fresh thinking, new perspectives, and exploring with energy, we’ll give you real responsibility and an opportunity to move with purpose from day one – putting the power to supercharge your career in your hands.

Graduates start their careers at National Grid with an in-depth 3-week in-person Orientation which gives you exposure to all parts of the company, allows you to network with your Graduate cohort, GDP alumni, and senior leaders, and provides you with the opportunity to travel throughout our service territory in the northeast US. Following Orientation, you’ll begin working in the full-time position outlined below and take part in robust in-person and virtual development activities throughout the year. This includes monthly development sessions, active mentorship, and an intensive and immersive “Hackathon Project” where you “hack” a real-world National Grid problem.

About National Grid

National Grid is the critical energy infrastructure company, operating the electricity and gas networks and infrastructures that connects millions of people to the energy they use every day, supporting homes, businesses and communities across Massachusetts and New York.

We know the future of energy won't be shaped by what we know today. It will be shaped by what's possible tomorrow. That's why we're investing in the next generation of talent, giving undergraduates and graduates the opportunity to learn from experts, gain hands-on experience and contribute to work that matters from day one.

Are you ready to unlock the power of the possible?

This individual will act as a vital link between sales leadership and technical teams, ensuring that platforms supporting field operations are optimized and efficiently managed.

As a high level delivery leader, you will be responsible for the roadmap and execution of systems involving territory management, incentive compensation, and CRM tools. The role combines the strategic oversight of a business partner with the hands on governance of an agile delivery lead.

Primary Responsibilities

Direct the requirements strategy for all field sales platforms, ensuring the business analysis team produces high quality documentation and sprint ready user stories.

Manage agile ceremonies and scrum governance, maintaining clear visibility of progress via Jira for all major stakeholders.

Serve as a strategic advisor to sales operations and field leadership, helping to shape the technology roadmap based on user feedback and industry trends.

Lead cross functional teams to ensure that platform changes, data models, and rep facing tools are functional and scalable.

Manage risks and proactively address any issues that could impact field sales operations or data quality.

Facilitate continuous improvement by reviewing delivery practices and establishing high standards for business analysis across the department.

Required Qualifications

At least ten years of experience in business analysis or IT delivery, with a background in people management within a matrixed environment.

Deep technical knowledge of pharmaceutical field sales platforms such as Veeva CRM, territory alignment tools, or call planning systems.

Significant experience as a Scrum Master or Agile Lead, with proficiency in using Jira for backlog and sprint management.

Strong background in requirements elicitation and the creation of functional specifications and process maps.

Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence senior executives and commercial stakeholders.

Specific experience in pharmaceutical commercialization and field sales operations is essential.

Education

A Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business, or Life Sciences is required, while an advanced degree is considered a plus.

Compensation and Benefits

This position offers a competitive salary range starting between 150,000 and 181,000 depending on experience and location.
