new_jobs.description:
About The Role

Lead the delivery of major infrastructure projects that will help shape the future of Britain's electricity network.

At National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET), we're delivering one of the largest investment programmes in a generation. As demand for electricity increases and new technologies transform the way we live and work, we're building the network needed to connect cleaner energy, support economic growth and power the UK's future.

As a Senior Project Manager, you'll lead and develop a team of Project Managers responsible for delivering a diverse portfolio of major infrastructure and customer connection projects across London. These projects play a critical role in enabling the UK's energy transition and digital growth, from connecting large-scale data centres supporting AI and emerging technologies, to delivering transmission network reinforcements, substations, HVDC projects, battery storage and renewable energy connections.

This is a highly visible leadership role with responsibility for both project delivery and people leadership. You'll provide direction, support and challenge to your team, ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the highest standards while creating an environment where people can develop and perform at their best.

Working across the full project lifecycle, you'll oversee the successful progression of projects from initial funding and optioneering through design, procurement, contract award, construction and commissioning. You'll work closely with internal and external stakeholders, delivery partners and contractors to manage risk, drive performance and achieve successful outcomes.

You'll also help shape how we deliver projects in the future, championing continuous improvement, strengthening collaboration across teams and sharing best practice across the wider business.

The scale, complexity and significance of this work is exceptional. Every project you deliver will help connect the customers, technologies and low-carbon energy sources that are driving the UK's future, leaving a lasting impact on the electricity network and the communities it serves.

Projects are located across London, so you'll need to be within commuting distance. The role combines time in project and site offices with travel throughout the region, alongside ad hoc home working.

What you'll bring

We're looking for an experienced project leader who combines strong delivery capability with the ability to motivate, develop and lead high-performing teams.

You'll bring:

Significant experience delivering complex construction, infrastructure, utilities or energy projects through design, procurement, delivery and commissioning.
Strong commercial and contractual management experience, with the ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and delivery partners to achieve successful project outcomes.
Experience managing projects within complex stakeholder environments and significant capital investment programmes.
A strong understanding of portfolio-level financial planning, forecasting and performance reporting.
Experience overseeing supply chain and contractor performance throughout the construction phase.
Sound knowledge of CDM regulations, health, safety and environmental requirements.
The ability to identify, assess and manage project risks while making informed decisions in a changing environment.
A proactive and collaborative leadership style, with a track record of developing people and building high-performing teams.
Experience gained within a client, contractor, utility, infrastructure or customer environment.

Ideally, you'll hold a qualification in Project Management, Engineering or a related discipline (or have equivalent experience) and possess a full UK driving licence.

What you'll get

A competitive salary between £70,000 - £86,000 – dependent on capability.
An annual performance bonus of up to 30% of your eligible earnings in the performance year.
Job requirement company car.
28 days annual leave plus eight statutory days.
The option to buy additional or sell holiday days.
A generous contributory pension scheme - we will double-match your contribution to a maximum company contribution of 12%.
Financial support to help cover the cost of professional membership subscriptions, course fees, books, exam fees and time off for study leave - so long as it's relevant to your role.
Access to flexible benefits such as a share incentive plan, salary sacrifice car and technology schemes, support via employee assistance lines and matched charity giving to name a few.
Family care benefits including a back-up care service for when your usual care arrangements fall through (six paid days each year as standard with the option to purchase further days).
Access to apps that support health, fitness and wellbeing.

More information

This role closes on 22 November 2026 at 23:59
, however we encourage candidates to submit their application as early as possible and not wait until the published closing date as this can vary. Interviews will be held in person in Central London on 3 and 4 December 2026.

We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates – we make appointments purely on merit, assessed against objective selection criteria. We support flexible working and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process should you have any physical or mental impairment which may affect your ability to participate in the process.

Please note that in most cases, National Grid is unable to offer sponsorship for employment under the UK points-based immigration system. As such, applicants must have the legal right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship now or in the future under the UK points-based immigration system. However, in exceptional circumstances where there is a clear and demonstrable need for specialist skills that cannot be sourced from the local labour market, National Grid may consider offering sponsorship. All applications are welcome from candidates who meet these requirements, regardless of race, nationality, or ethnic origin.

new_jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

Supply Chain Programme Manager

🛠️ About Our Supply Chain Team

The Supply Chain Programme Manager is a critical cross-functional role responsible for owning end-to-end supply chain execution across assigned programmes and product builds at Wayve. This includes prototype development, new product introduction (NPI) and supporting fleet launches.

You’ll serve as the primary Supply Chain lead for your programmes, ensuring programme deliverables, supplier compliance and seamless coordination across Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing and external partners. You’ll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance, Legal and Suppliers, while partnering closely with global upfitters and third-party integration partners across the US, UK and other regions to ensure vehicle and programme timelines are met.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll own end-to-end material readiness across assigned programmes, translating engineering requirements and demand into procurement plans and identifying supply risks early in the product lifecycle.

You’ll operate as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement, coordinating internal teams, suppliers, upfitters and integration partners to keep builds moving. This role combines strategic programme ownership with hands-on execution in a fast-moving, hardware-driven environment.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Acting as the primary Supply Chain lead for assigned programmes and internal product builds, including prototypes, NPI and subassemblies.
Owning end-to-end material readiness to support programme milestones across R&D, Engineering, Operations and Manufacturing.
Collaborating with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance and Suppliers to align supply chain activities with programme timelines.
Acting as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement teams, including managing demand aggregation.
Translating engineering BOMs and aggregated Technical Programme Manager demand into procurement plans.
Identifying long-lead items and critical-path components early in the product lifecycle.
Tracking material status throughout build phases and proactively escalating gaps and risks.
Serving as the primary programme manager for upfitter and partner relationships, ensuring alignment across stakeholders.
Driving upfitter and partner activities to ensure vehicles meet overall programme timelines and quality standards.
Proactively identifying and resolving issues affecting vehicle build readiness, coordinating between internal teams and external partners.
Maintaining clear communication cadences with upfitters and stakeholders, tracking milestones and escalating risks as needed.
Defining, tracking and reporting key supply chain performance metrics, including material availability, total cost savings and inventory cycle count accuracy.
Establishing programme-level supply chain dashboards and reporting cadences to provide leadership and cross-functional stakeholders with visibility.
Analysing KPI trends to identify root causes of supply chain underperformance and driving corrective actions with suppliers and internal teams.
Using KPI insights to continuously improve supply chain processes, reduce waste and increase overall programme efficiency.
Collaborating with Supply Chain Team Leads to ensure direct purchasing, indirect purchasing and logistics suppliers meet compliance requirements, including legal, environmental, regulatory requirements such as TISAX and ISO, and ethical sourcing standards.
Partnering with Legal and Compliance teams to ensure appropriate supplier agreements, NDAs and risk controls are in place.
Developing contingency plans for supply disruptions and actively managing supply chain risks.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You have 10+ years of progressive experience in supply chain programme management, NPI and hardware operations.
You have a strong understanding of BOM management, material planning and procurement processes.
You have demonstrated experience managing cross-functional programmes across Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain.
You bring strong analytical, problem-solving and risk-management skills.
You have excellent communication and stakeholder-management capabilities.
You are able to travel internally as needed.
Experience in the automotive, consumer, hardware or robotics industries is preferred.
Familiarity with supplier compliance frameworks, including TISAX, ISO standards and ethical sourcing requirements, is preferred.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay!
If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻 – Locations & Flexible Working:

This is a full-time, office-based role located in London
, depending on the candidate’s place of residence.

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our offices and workshops with focused time working remotely. We also operate core working hours so you can determine the schedule that works best for you and your team.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency interviews (Hiring Manager Interview) (45 mins)
Deep-dive interviews (Team and Cross-functional Interviews) (3 hrs)
Final interview (30 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s In It For You

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

new_jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

Supply Chain Program Manager

🛠️ About Our Supply Chain Team

The Supply Chain Program Manager is a critical cross-functional role responsible for owning end-to-end supply chain execution across assigned programs and product builds at Wayve, including prototype development, new product introduction (NPI), and fleet launches.

You’ll serve as the primary Supply Chain lead for your programs, ensuring program deliverables, supplier compliance and seamless coordination across Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing and external partners. You’ll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance, Legal and Suppliers, while partnering closely with global upfitters and third-party integration partners across the US, UK and other regions to keep vehicle and program timelines on track.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll own end-to-end material readiness across assigned programs, translating engineering requirements and demand into actionable procurement plans and identifying supply risks early in the product lifecycle.

You’ll operate as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement, coordinating internal teams, suppliers, upfitters and integration partners to keep builds moving. You’ll combine strategic program ownership with hands-on execution—tracking materials, resolving readiness issues, managing supply chain risk and using KPIs to drive continuous improvement.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Acting as the primary Supply Chain lead for assigned programs and internal product builds, including prototypes, NPI and subassemblies.
Owning end-to-end material readiness to support program milestones across R&D, Engineering, Operations and Manufacturing.
Collaborating with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance and Suppliers to align supply chain activities with program timelines.
Acting as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement teams, including managing demand aggregation.
Translating engineering BOMs and aggregated Technical Program Manager demand into procurement plans.
Identifying long-lead items and critical-path components early in the product lifecycle, tracking material status throughout build phases and proactively escalating gaps and risks.
Collaborating with Supply Chain Team Leads to ensure direct purchasing, indirect purchasing and logistics suppliers meet legal, environmental, regulatory and ethical sourcing requirements, including TISAX and ISO standards.
Partnering with Legal and Compliance to ensure appropriate supplier agreements, NDAs and risk controls are in place.
Developing contingency plans for supply disruptions and actively managing supply chain risks.
Serving as the primary program manager for upfitter and partner relationships, maintaining stakeholder alignment and driving activities against vehicle timelines and quality standards.
Proactively identifying and resolving issues affecting vehicle build readiness while coordinating internal teams and external partners.
Maintaining clear communication cadences with upfitters and stakeholders, tracking milestones and escalating risks as needed.
Defining, tracking and reporting supply chain KPIs, including material availability, total cost savings and inventory cycle count accuracy.
Establishing program-level dashboards and reporting cadences that provide leadership and cross-functional stakeholders with visibility into performance.
Analysing KPI trends to identify root causes of underperformance and drive corrective actions with suppliers and internal teams.
Using KPI insights to continuously improve supply chain processes, reduce waste and increase overall program efficiency.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You have 10+ years of progressive experience in supply chain program management, NPI and hardware operations.
You have a strong understanding of BOM management, material planning and procurement processes.
You have demonstrated experience managing cross-functional programs across Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain.
You bring strong analytical, problem-solving and risk-management skills.
You have excellent communication and stakeholder-management capabilities.
You are able to travel internationally as needed.
Experience in the automotive, consumer, hardware or robotics industries is preferred.
Familiarity with supplier compliance frameworks, including TISAX, ISO standards and ethical sourcing requirements, is preferred.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay!
If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻 – Locations & Flexible Working:

This is a full-time role based in Sunnyvale, CA (hybrid)
. The reasonably estimated salary range for this role is $184,200–$240,000, plus a competitive equity package
. Actual compensation is based on the candidate’s skills, qualifications and experience.

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces and workshops with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work. We also operate core working hours so you can determine the schedule that works best for you and your team.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency interviews (Hiring Manager Interview) (45 mins)
Deep-dive interviews (Team and cross-functional interviews) (3 hrs)
Final interview (30 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s In It For You

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.
